definition_zh: 污染物；沾染物；使某物变得不纯或不宜使用的物质
definition_en: a substance that makes something impure, unsafe or unfit for its intended use by being present in it
core_image: 取样瓶里浮着一层薄薄的油膜，原本清澈的水面被这一点外来物搅得不再可信
scene: 检测员在水厂的取样瓶里发现一层薄薄的油膜，仪器读数随即报警。 A single contaminant in the sample pushed the reading past the safety limit.
sceneCN: 这里 contaminant 指「混入某物、使其不纯或不宜使用的物质」（第 1 个义项：外来的沾染物使整体失去纯净）；句意为样本中一种污染物就把读数推过了安全限值。图中可辨识物件：取样瓶、油膜、检测仪、报警灯。

pos.zh: 污染物；沾染物（可数，指一种具体的污染物质）

senses.title: A substance that makes something impure
senses.titleCN: 使某物变得不纯的外来物质
senses.definition: any substance whose presence spoils the purity or quality of a material, medium or product
senses.definitionCN: 任何因其存在而破坏材料、介质或产品纯度与品质的物质
senses.example: A single contaminant in the sample pushed the reading past the safety limit.
senses.exampleCN: 样本中一种污染物就把读数推过了安全限值。
senses.why: The Latin root means 'to touch together', so a contaminant is literally something that has touched a clean body and left itself behind in it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「接触在一起」，因此 contaminant 字面上就是「碰过洁净之物并在其中留下自己的东西」。

senses.title: A pollutant in air, water or soil
senses.titleCN: 空气、水体或土壤中的污染物质
senses.definition: a substance present in an environmental medium at a level that harms organisms or uses
senses.definitionCN: 存在于环境介质中、其含量足以危害生物或用途的物质
senses.example: The aquifer held a solvent contaminant from the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 含水层里存着老工厂留下的一种溶剂污染物。
senses.why: Environmental science adopted the word because it names the thing rather than the harm, which is measured separately.
senses.whyCN: 环境科学采用这个词，因为它命名的是物质本身，而危害另有指标衡量。

senses.title: A biological contaminant such as a microbe
senses.titleCN: 微生物等生物性沾染物
senses.definition: a bacterium, virus, fungus or other organism that makes a product or surface unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 使产品或表面变得不安全的细菌、病毒、真菌或其他生物
senses.example: A bacterial contaminant closed the production line for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一种细菌污染物让生产线停了一周。
senses.why: Living things contaminate as effectively as chemicals, and laboratories needed one word that covers both.
senses.whyCN: 活物与化学品一样能造成沾染，实验室需要一个词同时涵盖两者。

senses.title: A trace residue of chemicals
senses.definition: a pesticide, drug, heavy metal or solvent left at very low concentration in food, water or tissue
senses.definitionCN: 以极低浓度残留在食品、水或组织中的农药、药物、重金属或溶剂
senses.example: Regulators set a limit for each pesticide contaminant.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构为每种农药残留设定了限值。
senses.why: Modern instruments can find a few parts per billion, so the word now covers amounts far too small to see.
senses.whyCN: 现代仪器能检出十亿分之几，这个词于是涵盖了肉眼完全看不见的量。

senses.title: Foreign matter in food or medicine
senses.titleCN: 食品与药品中的外来异物
senses.definition: glass, metal, plastic or other matter that enters a product during handling and makes it unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 在加工过程中进入产品、使其不安全的玻璃、金属、塑料或其他物质
senses.example: A metal contaminant triggered the recall of the batch.
senses.exampleCN: 一种金属污染物触发了这批产品的召回。
senses.why: For manufacturers the word covers anything that should not be in the package, living or not.
senses.whyCN: 对制造商而言，这个词涵盖一切不该出现在包装里的东西，无论是否有生命。

senses.title: A radioactive contaminant
senses.definition: a radionuclide deposited on a surface, in soil or in a body where it does not belong
senses.definitionCN: 沉积在不该出现的表面、土壤或人体内的放射性核素
senses.example: Workers mapped the radioactive contaminant around the old reactor.
senses.exampleCN: 工作人员标出了旧反应堆周围的放射性污染物。
senses.why: Radiation is invisible and persistent, so the word stresses location and unwanted presence rather than visible dirt.
senses.whyCN: 辐射看不见又持久，这个词于是强调位置与「不该在此」，而非看得见的脏污。

senses.title: A particle in a cleanroom or vacuum
senses.titleCN: 洁净室或真空中的微粒沾染物
senses.definition: a dust particle, fibre or molecular film that ruins a wafer, lens or vacuum process
senses.definitionCN: 使晶圆、镜片或真空工艺失效的尘粒、纤维或分子膜
senses.example: A sub-micron contaminant ruined the coating on the lens.
senses.exampleCN: 一粒亚微米级污染物毁掉了镜片镀膜。
senses.why: In manufacturing the threshold is not health but function: a particle too small to see can still break a circuit.
senses.whyCN: 在制造中，门槛不是健康而是功能：小到看不见的颗粒仍能毁掉电路。

senses.title: Abstract: anything that corrupts a clean system
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何使洁净系统失真的东西
senses.definition: a transferred use for an element that corrupts the purity of data, language or a process
senses.definitionCN: 转指使数据、语言或流程丧失纯净性的因素
senses.example: A stale record is a contaminant in the training set.
senses.exampleCN: 过时记录是训练集里的一种污染。
senses.why: The metaphor works because the physical image is general: a small foreign thing enters a clean body and changes what the body can be used for.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，是因为物理意象很通用：一小点外来物进入洁净的整体，改变了这个整体还能做什么。

intro.en: Contaminant is the noun use of the present participle of contaminate, which came to English from Latin by way of French. The root image is touching. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: contaminant 是 contaminate 现在分词的名词化用法，而 contaminate 经法语来自拉丁语。其词根意象是「接触」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tangere meant 'to touch'. Its deeper origin is not established; the Indo-European root often proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: tangere 意为「触摸」。其更深来源未得到证明；常为它提出的印欧词根是重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus the touch root produced contamen 'contact, pollution', the idea of one thing being defiled by touching another.
items.cn: com-「共同」加「触摸」词根构成 contamen「接触、污染」，即一物因碰到另一物而被弄脏。

items.en: Contaminare meant 'to defile by contact, to corrupt'. It carried both the physical and the moral sense of making something unclean.
items.cn: contaminare 意为「因接触而弄脏、败坏」。它同时带有「使不洁」的物理义与道德义。

items.en: English contaminate appears in the sixteenth century, first of moral or ritual defilement and later of physical mixture.
items.cn: 英语 contaminate 出现于十六世纪，先指道德或仪式上的玷污，后指物理上的混入。

items.en: Contaminant became a separate noun in modern technical English, once laboratories needed a word for the offending substance itself rather than the act.
items.cn: 当实验室需要一个词来指「肇事的物质本身」而非动作时，contaminant 在现代技术英语中成为独立名词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date of the noun, deeper origin of tangere): the noun's first technical citation is not fixed, so its date is approximate; the pre-Latin origin of tangere is unsettled and any form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（该名词的首见年代、tangere 的更深词源）：这个名词最早的 technical 书证没有定论，年代只能约计；tangere 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，凡为其提出的形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same touch-root family that are easily mistaken for the noun; group two holds other words for unwanted material, each with a different reason for being unwanted.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「触摸」词根、容易被误当作本名词的各种形式；第二组是其他表示「不该有的物质」的词，各自「不该有」的理由不同。

entries.definition: The act or result of contaminating; it names the event or condition, while contaminant names the substance.
entries.definitionCN: 污染的动作或结果；它指事件或状态，而 contaminant 指物质。

entries.definition: To make impure by contact; it is the action that puts a contaminant into something.
entries.definitionCN: 因接触而使不纯；它是把污染物放进某物的动作。

entries.definition: Touching or communication, from the same tangere root but with no sense of defilement.
entries.definitionCN: 接触或联系，同出 tangere 词根，但不含「玷污」之义。

entries.definition: Spread of disease by contact, from contingere 'to touch upon'; it shares the touch root but follows a medical path.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病经接触传播，出自 contingere「触及」；它与 contaminant 同享触摸词根，却走的是医学路线。

entries.definition: A substance that harms the environment; a contaminant may be harmless in small amounts and still unfit a product.
entries.definitionCN: 危害环境的物质；污染物质量小时可能无害，却仍能使产品不合格。

entries.definition: Any foreign matter in a material, often harmless; it is a purity term rather than a safety term.
entries.definitionCN: 材料中混入的任何外来物，常为无害；它是纯度术语，而非安全术语。

entries.definition: A substance that is poisonous to living things; toxicity is its defining property, which a contaminant need not have.
entries.definitionCN: 对生物有毒的物质；毒性是它的定义属性，而污染物不一定有毒。

entries.definition: Something added to a product to cheapen or fake it; the motive is deception, not accidental mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 为降低成本或造假而加入产品的东西；其动机是欺骗，而非意外混入。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is tangere 'to touch': something touched the clean body and stayed in it.
normal.cn: 词根是 tangere「触摸」：某物碰过洁净之物并留在了里面。

normal.en: Contaminant is the thing, contamination is the process, contaminate is the act.
normal.cn: contaminant 是物，contamination 是过程，contaminate 是动作。

normal.en: The family runs contaminate, contamination, contaminated, decontaminate and contaminative.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 contaminate、contamination、contaminated、decontaminate 与 contaminative。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: chemical contaminant, biological contaminant, trace contaminant.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：化学污染物、生物污染物、痕量污染物。

normal.en: Contact and contagion share the touch root but carry no idea of impurity in the same way.
normal.cn: contact 与 contagion 共享触摸词根，但并不以同样的方式带有「不纯」之意。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of ink falling into a glass of clear water.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴墨落进一杯清水。

abstract.en: Picture a single wrong figure entering an otherwise clean ledger.
abstract.cn: 想象一个错数进入一本本来干净的账。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour passing through a room and changing what everyone repeats.
abstract.cn: 想象一则传言穿过一间屋子，改变了每个人复述的内容。

examples.en: The filter removes the contaminant before the water reaches the tap.
examples.cn: 过滤器在水到达龙头之前去除污染物。

examples.en: Each contaminant has its own detection limit and removal method.
examples.cn: 每种污染物都有自己的检出限与去除方法。

examples.en: A biological contaminant can multiply after it enters the product.
examples.cn: 生物污染物进入产品之后还可能增殖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「con（共同）+ tamin（接触）+ ant」——碰到干净东西、把它弄脏的那一位 → 污染物

root: 拉丁 contaminare「弄脏、败坏」< contamen「接触、污染」= com-（共同）+ tangere「触摸」；tangere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one intrusion: a foreign thing touches a clean body, purity is lost, fitness is lost, the intruder is measured, and finally the same shape is used for corrupted data.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次侵入展开：外来物碰触洁净体，纯净性失去，可用性失去，侵入者被计量，最后同一形态被用于被污染的数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one drop of oil floating in a bottle of clear water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一瓶清水里浮着一滴油。

branches.en: PURITY AND ENVIRONMENT: the general definition and the environmental case both name the intruder, not the harm.
branches.cn: 纯净与环境：总定义与环境情形命名的都是侵入者，而非危害。

branches.en: LIVING AND TRACE: a microbe and a residue are both small enough to escape the eye.
branches.cn: 活物与痕量：微生物与残留都小到肉眼难辨。

branches.en: PRODUCT SAFETY: what should never be in the package defines this sense.
branches.cn: 产品安全：本不该出现在包装里的东西，界定了这个义项。

branches.en: LOCATION AND FUNCTION: radiation in the wrong place and a particle in a cleanroom both ruin by being where they are.
branches.cn: 位置与功能：错处的辐射与洁净室里的颗粒，都因「待在那里」而毁事。

branches.en: TRANSFER: a bad record contaminates a dataset as oil contaminates water.
branches.cn: 转移：坏记录污染数据集，正如油污染水。

intro.en: Contaminant is a Latin-derived noun with a prefix, a touch root and a participial suffix, so it can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: contaminant 是拉丁来源名词，含前缀、触摸词根与分词后缀，可以逐语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin tangere 'to touch' gives contact, contagion, contiguous and tangible; con- adds 'together' and -ant marks the thing that does the action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tangere「触摸」衍生 contact、contagion、contiguous 与 tangible；con- 添「共同」，-ant 标出执行动作之物。

items.example: The prefix marks contact between two things.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出两物之间的接触。

items.example: The root carries the idea of contact.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「接触」的意思。

items.example: Contamen named the defilement left by touch.
items.exampleCN: contamen 指接触留下的污损。

items.example: The verb entered English as contaminate.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词以 contaminate 进入英语。

items.meaning: the thing or person that does
items.example: The suffix makes the verb into the offending thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成「肇事的物」。

items.example: One contaminant spoiled the whole tank.
items.exampleCN: 一种污染物毁掉了整罐。

items.meaning: the act or state of being defiled

items.exampleCN: 队伍对场地进行了去污。

items.example: The two surfaces were in contact.

definition_zh: 连贯性；一致性；连贯；相干性
definition_en: the quality of parts sticking together into a consistent whole, or of waves keeping a fixed phase relation
core_image: 几页散开的稿纸被一根线串在一起，每段都接住上一段留下的问题
scene: 编辑把散开的稿页按顺序串起，每段都接住上一段留下的问题。 Readers praised the coherence of the argument.
sceneCN: 这里指论证前后连成一体（第 1 个义项：逻辑一致性）；句意为读者称赞这篇论证的连贯。图中可辨识物件：稿纸、装订线、红笔、段落标记。

pos.zh: 名词：连贯性；一致性；相干性（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁词根加形容词词尾构成，义为「连贯的；一致的」
由该形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「连贯地」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「不连贯的」
由该否定形容词加名词词尾构成，义为「不连贯」
由同一词根的另一派生形式构成，义为「黏合；凝聚力」

senses.title: Logical consistency
senses.definition: the quality of an argument whose parts support one another without contradiction
senses.definitionCN: 论证各部分互相支撑、不相矛盾的性质
senses.example: Reviewers questioned the coherence of the argument in the final chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 审稿人质疑最后一章论证的连贯。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to stick together, so a coherent argument is one whose parts do not come apart.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「黏在一起」，因此连贯的论证就是各部分不会散开。

senses.title: For textual unity
senses.definition: the quality of a text whose sentences and paragraphs hold together as one piece
senses.definitionCN: 文章句子与段落合成一体的性质
senses.example: Clear signposting improves the coherence of a long report.
senses.exampleCN: 清晰的衔接语能改善长篇报告的连贯。
senses.why: Writing needs links that make the reader feel one hand behind many sentences.
senses.whyCN: 写作需要连接手段，让读者感到许多句子背后是同一只手。

senses.title: Coherence of a group
senses.definition: the quality of a group acting or thinking as a united body
senses.definitionCN: 群体作为一个整体行动或思考的性质
senses.example: The coalition lost coherence after the budget vote.
senses.exampleCN: 预算表决之后，这个联盟失去了凝聚力。
senses.why: A group whose members stick together is described with the same physical image.
senses.whyCN: 成员黏在一起的群体，用的还是同一个物理意象。

senses.title: Consistency of a plan or policy
senses.definition: the quality of measures fitting together without working against each other
senses.definitionCN: 各项措施彼此配合、不相冲突的性质
senses.example: The audit found little coherence between transport and housing policy.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现交通与住房政策之间缺乏一致。
senses.why: Measures that pull in different directions cannot stick together, so policy coherence is judged by mutual fit.
senses.whyCN: 相互拉扯的措施无法黏在一起，因此政策的一致要看彼此是否合得上。

senses.title: Coherence of waves and light
senses.definition: the fixed phase relation that lets waves interfere in a stable pattern
senses.definitionCN: 使波能形成稳定干涉图样的固定相位关系
senses.example: Lasers produce light with high coherence over long distances.
senses.exampleCN: 激光在长距离上产生高相干性的光。
senses.why: Physics kept the original image: waves that stay in step are literally sticking together.
senses.whyCN: 物理学保留原意象：步伐一致的波，字面上就是黏在一起。

senses.title: Discourse coherence in linguistics
senses.definition: the property that makes a stretch of discourse interpretable as a single message
senses.definitionCN: 使一段话语可被理解为单一信息的性质
senses.example: The study compares coherence across spoken and written registers.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究比较口语与书面语域中的连贯。
senses.why: Linguistics separates the surface ties from the deeper sense of one message.
senses.whyCN: 语言学把表层的连接手段与深层的一条信息区分开。

senses.title: Optical coherence
senses.definition: the property of light that allows stable interference fringes to form
senses.definitionCN: 光能形成稳定干涉条纹的性质
senses.example: The instrument measures coherence between two reflected beams.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器测量两束反射光之间的相干性。
senses.why: Two beams are coherent when their crests and troughs keep a fixed relationship.
senses.whyCN: 两束光的波峰与波谷保持固定关系时，就是相干的。

senses.title: Narrative coherence
senses.definition: the quality of a story whose events and motives fit into one believable line
senses.definitionCN: 故事的事件与动机串成一条可信线索的性质
senses.example: The memoir achieves narrative coherence by returning to one image.
senses.exampleCN: 这部回忆录靠反复回到同一个意象获得叙事连贯。
senses.why: A story sticks together when each event can be read as following from the last.
senses.whyCN: 当每个事件都能读作由上一个事件引出时，故事就黏住了。

senses.title: Coherence of a legal system
senses.definition: the quality of rules in a system fitting together without contradiction
senses.definitionCN: 体系中各项规则彼此配合、不相矛盾的性质
senses.example: Judges appealed to the coherence of the statute as a whole.
senses.exampleCN: 法官援引整部法规的一致性。
senses.why: Legal theory asks whether rules can be read as one consistent scheme.
senses.whyCN: 法学理论追问各项规则能否被读成一个前后一致的方案。

intro.en: Coherence comes from Latin cohaerere, to stick together, built from co-, together, and haerere, to stick or cling. The Latin noun cohaerentia passed through French into English in the sixteenth century, first for physical joining and later for logic.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 cohaerere「黏在一起」，由表示「共同」的前缀与表示「黏附」的词根构成。拉丁名词经法语在十六世纪进入英语，先指物理上的接合，后来才指逻辑上的连贯。

items.en: The verb meant to stick, cling or be fixed, and it also stands behind adhere and hesitate.
items.cn: 这个动词意为黏附、贴住、固定，也是「附着」与「犹豫」二词的源头。

items.en: The prefix meant together or with, and it turns sticking into sticking together.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为共同、一起，把「黏」变成「黏在一起」。

items.en: The compound meant to hold together as one mass, used of bodies and later of ideas.
items.cn: 这个复合动词意为合成一体地连着，先用于物体，后用于观念。

items.en: The noun named the state of holding together.
items.cn: 这个名词指「连成一体」的状态。

items.en: The noun entered English through French in the sixteenth century, first for physical connection.
items.cn: 这个名词经法语在十六世纪进入英语，最初指物理连接。

items.en: Philosophy extended it to arguments and texts, where parts must hold together in meaning.
items.cn: 哲学把它扩展到论证与文本，要求各部分在意义上连成一体。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root or its negative; the second group names similar unities.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根或其否定形式；第二组是类似的统一性质。

entries.definition: The adjective for sticking together logically.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为连贯的、一致的。

entries.definition: In a connected and consistent way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以连贯一致的方式。

entries.definition: Not holding together; confused in expression.
entries.definitionCN: 指不连贯、表述混乱的。

entries.definition: The noun for a failure to hold together.
entries.definitionCN: 指无法连成一体的状态。

entries.definition: The act of sticking together, especially of groups or text surfaces.
entries.definitionCN: 指黏合，多用于群体或文本表层。

entries.definition: The quality of not contradicting itself over time.
entries.definitionCN: 指前后不自相矛盾的性质。

entries.definition: The state of being one whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指成为一体的状态。

entries.definition: Unbroken connection from one part to the next.
entries.definitionCN: 指各部分之间不断裂的连接。

entries.definition: The structure of valid reasoning itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指有效推理的结构本身。

entries.definition: Surface linking between sentences, distinct from deeper coherence.
entries.definitionCN: 指句子表层的连接，与更深层的连贯有别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations begin with the literal image of sticking together, then follow it into writing, groups, policy and light.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想从「黏在一起」的字面意象出发，再走到文章、群体、政策与光。

normal.en: The root verb means to stick, so coherent parts do not fall apart under pressure.
normal.cn: 词根意为黏附，所以连贯的各部分受力也不会散开。

normal.en: Signposting words are the visible glue of a long report.
normal.cn: 衔接词是长篇报告上看得见的胶水。

normal.en: A coalition that sticks together after a lost vote has coherence in the group sense.
normal.cn: 表决失利后仍黏在一起的联盟，具备群体意义上的凝聚。

normal.en: Lasers are the clearest physical case: their waves stay in step, so they are coherent.
normal.cn: 激光是最清楚的物理例子：波保持同步，所以相干。

normal.en: Legal theory asks whether separate rules can be read as one scheme.
normal.cn: 法学理论追问分开的规则能否被读成一个方案。

abstract.en: Coherence is what makes many sentences feel like one voice in the room.
abstract.cn: 连贯让许多句子听起来像房间里同一个人的声音。

abstract.en: Two ideas can both be true and still lack coherence, because truth is not gluing.
abstract.cn: 两个想法可以都真却仍不连贯，因为真并不等于黏合。

abstract.en: Every whole is held together by something invisible, and this word names that hold.
abstract.cn: 每个整体都靠某种看不见的东西连住，这个词给那份「连」命名。

examples.en: The editor rewrote two paragraphs to restore coherence.
examples.cn: 编辑改写了两段，以恢复连贯。

examples.en: Coherence between the two policies was missing from the start.
examples.cn: 这两项政策从一开始就缺乏一致。

examples.en: The laboratory measures coherence in a beam of light.
examples.cn: 实验室测量一束光的相干性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「扣希尔伦斯」——许多段被同一根线扣在一起，就是「连贯、一致」：连贯性、一致性

root: 这个词来自拉丁语 cohaerere「黏在一起」，由表示「共同」的前缀与 haerere「黏附」构成；拉丁名词经法语在十六世纪进入英语，先指物理连接，后指逻辑与语篇的连贯。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses hold the same image of sticking together, applied to argument, text, group, policy, light, discourse, optics, story and law.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共用一个「黏在一起」的意象，分别用在论证、文本、群体、政策、光、话语、光学、故事与法律上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose sheets threaded by one cord, each paragraph picking up the question the last left open.
core.cn: 核心意象：散页被一根线串起，每段接住上一段留下的问题。

branches.en: THE JOINED ARGUMENT AND THE JOINED LAW: claims and rules must not contradict each other.
branches.cn: 连起的论证与连起的法律：主张与规则不得彼此矛盾。

branches.en: THE JOINED TEXT AND DISCOURSE: sentences and utterances read as one message.
branches.cn: 连起的文本与话语：句子与话语被读成一条信息。

branches.en: THE JOINED GROUP AND POLICY: members and measures hold as one body.
branches.cn: 连起的群体与政策：成员与措施合成一体。

branches.en: THE WAVES IN STEP: a fixed phase relation makes stable interference possible.
branches.cn: 同步的波：固定相位关系使稳定干涉成为可能。

branches.en: THE JOINED STORY: events and motives form one believable line.
branches.cn: 连起的故事：事件与动机构成一条可信线索。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of sticking with a prefix of togetherness, and English added a noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示「黏附」的拉丁动词加上表示「共同」的前缀，英语再加名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the verb of sticking, the prefix of togetherness, the compound verb and its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示黏附的动词、表示共同的前缀、复合动词及其名词。

items.example: It also stands behind adhere and hesitate.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「附着」与「犹豫」二词的源头。

items.example: It turns sticking into sticking together.
The verb describes parts that do not separate.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述不会分开的各部分。

items.example: The noun named the state before English borrowed it.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词在英语借入前已指该状态。

items.example: English extended it from bodies to arguments.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它从物体扩展到论证。

items.example: The adjective adds a Latin adjective ending.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词加了拉丁形容词词尾。
它标记类似分词的形容词。
它构成表示「散开」的形容词。

items.example: The sibling noun stresses the bond itself.
items.exampleCN: 同族名词更强调黏合本身。

加副词词尾构成，义为「连贯地」

definition_zh: 监督者；主管；导师；（美国部分地区的）县政委员；监考人
definition_en: a person who watches over other workers or a process and is responsible for it
core_image: 一个站在工序尽头的人，手里拿着清单，逐项核对刚做完的东西
scene: 流水线末端的检查台上，每件成品都要经过同一个人复核，合格才盖章。 A supervisor checks the last item before the line stops for the night.
sceneCN: 这里 supervisor 指对他人工作或流程负监督之责的人（第 1 个义项：直接看管工人的人）；句意：产线夜里停工前，主管检查最后一件产品。图中可辨识物件：检查台、成品、印章、交接记录。

pos.zh: 监督者；主管；导师；监考人；（美国）县政委员

senses.title: The one who watches the workers
senses.definition: a person whose job is to watch other workers and see that the work is done properly
senses.definitionCN: 受雇看住其他工人并确保工作做好的那个人
senses.example: The supervisor stopped the line when she saw the wrong label.
senses.exampleCN: 主管看到标签贴错，就叫停了产线。
senses.why: The word is the agent form of supervise, so it names the eye that sits above the work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 supervise 的施动形式，命名的是悬在工作上方的那只眼。

senses.title: Head of a shift or unit
senses.titleCN: 一个班次或单元的主管
senses.definition: the person in charge of one shift, counter or small unit during working hours
senses.definitionCN: 在工作时段内负责一个班次、柜台或小单元的人
senses.example: The night-shift supervisor counts the keys before handing over.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班主管在交接前清点钥匙。
senses.why: A shift is a closed block of time, and one person must answer for that block.
senses.whyCN: 一个班次是一段封闭的时间，必须有人为这一段负责。

senses.title: Academic research adviser
senses.definition: a teacher who guides a student's research and approves its progress
senses.definitionCN: 指导学生研究并核可其进度的一位教师
senses.example: Her supervisor asked for a shorter literature review.
senses.exampleCN: 她的导师要求把文献综述写短一些。
senses.why: Research has no shift and no counter, so the same eye is lent to one student for years.
senses.whyCN: 研究没有班次也没有柜台，于是同一只眼借给一个学生好几年。

senses.title: An elected county official
senses.definition: in some American states, an elected member of a county's governing board
senses.definitionCN: 在美国某些州，县管理委员会的民选成员
senses.example: The county supervisor voted against the new landfill.
senses.exampleCN: 那位县政委员投票反对新建填埋场。
senses.why: Local government borrowed the title for an officer who watches over county business.
senses.whyCN: 地方政府借用了这个称号，指看管县务的官员。

senses.title: An examination invigilator
senses.definition: the person who watches candidates during an examination
senses.definitionCN: 考试期间看住考生的人
senses.example: The supervisor read the rules before opening the envelopes.
senses.exampleCN: 监考人在拆封前宣读了考场规则。
senses.why: An exam is a guarded room, and the guard is called by the watching word.
senses.whyCN: 考场是一个被守住的房间，守门人就用那个表示「看」的词来称呼。

senses.title: A program that controls other programs
senses.definition: a controlling program that starts, stops and watches other processes
senses.definitionCN: 负责启动、停止并监视其他进程的控制程序
senses.example: The supervisor restarts any worker that crashes.
senses.exampleCN: 监控程序会重启任何崩溃的工作进程。
senses.why: When software took over the watching, the name of the person passed to the program.
senses.whyCN: 当软件接手「看管」，人的名称就传给了程序。

senses.title: The hospital officer who allocates beds
senses.titleCN: 在医院调度床位与人员的主管
senses.definition: the nursing officer who coordinates beds and staffing across a hospital at night
senses.definitionCN: 夜间统筹全院床位与护理人力的护理主管
senses.example: The house supervisor found a bed for the second ambulance.
senses.exampleCN: 值班主管为第二辆救护车找到了床位。
senses.why: A whole hospital at night is one closed block, and one watching officer keeps it balanced.
senses.whyCN: 夜里的整座医院是一个封闭单元，由一位值班主管让它保持平衡。

senses.title: A visit monitor in social services
senses.titleCN: 社会福利中监督探视的人
senses.definition: a person who watches a court-ordered family visit to keep everyone safe
senses.definitionCN: 在法院指定的家庭探视中在场监督、保障各方安全的人
senses.example: A supervisor sat in the corner during the two-hour visit.
senses.exampleCN: 两小时的探视中，一位监督员坐在角落。
senses.why: Here the eye protects rather than judges, which is the guarding side of the same word.
senses.whyCN: 这里的眼睛是保护而非评判，这正是同一个词里「守护」的那一面。

intro.en: Supervisor is the agent noun of supervise, from Medieval Latin supervisus 'looked over'. Its many job senses all keep one picture: an eye placed above a piece of work.
intro.cn: supervisor 是 supervise 的施动名词，源自中世纪拉丁 supervisus「被巡视过的」。它的众多职位义都保留同一个画面：一只眼悬在一项工作的上方。

items.en: Videre 'to see' gives the vis- of supervisor, and also vision and visible.
items.cn: videre「看见」提供了 supervisor 里的 vis-，也提供 vision 与 visible。

items.en: Super 'above' places the watcher higher than the watched, which is why the title carries authority.
items.cn: super「在上」把看的人放在被看者之上，因此这个称号带有权力。

items.en: Supervidere 'to inspect' produced the participle supervisus and the agent form supervisor in medieval Latin.
items.cn: supervidere「检查」在中世纪拉丁产生分词 supervisus 与施动形式 supervisor。

items.en: Supervisor appears in English in the sixteenth century, at first for an inspector of work; the earliest date is approximate.
items.cn: supervisor 在十六世纪出现于英语，最初指工作的检查者；最早年代为约数。

items.en: County boards, hospitals and computing gave the title new offices in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 县政委员会、医院与计算机在十九、二十世纪赋予这个称号新的职位。

note.en: The first group shares the supervise root or a near shape; the second group names other people who check work.
note.cn: 第一组共享 supervise 词根或形音相近；第二组是其他核查工作的人。

entries.definition: The verb, naming the activity rather than the person.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指活动而不是人。

entries.definition: The activity or the state of being watched over.
entries.definitionCN: 指监督活动或被监督的状态。

entries.definition: The adjective describing the role or its powers.
entries.definitionCN: 描述该角色或其权力的形容词。

entries.definition: From the same Latin verb, but the person measures land rather than staff.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个拉丁动词，但此人是丈量土地，不是看人。

entries.definition: Runs a unit and its results; a supervisor may only check that rules are kept.
entries.definitionCN: 经营一个单元及其成果；主管可能只核查规则是否遵守。

entries.definition: The English-rooted word for the same role, often on plantations or worksites.
entries.definitionCN: 同一角色的英语本族词，常用于种植园或工地。

entries.definition: The working leader of a gang of manual workers.
entries.definitionCN: 一组体力工人中带班的领头人。

entries.definition: The British title for the person who watches an examination.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语中监考人的称号。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real agent suffix, the real family and real job titles.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的施动后缀、真实的同族词与真实的职位名称。

normal.en: Supervise plus -or gives supervisor, literally the one who looks over.
normal.cn: supervise 加施动后缀得到 supervisor，字面上就是「在上方看的那一个」。

normal.en: The family runs supervise, supervision, supervisory and supervisorship.
normal.cn: 同族词有 supervise、supervision、supervisory 与 supervisorship。

normal.en: Titles show the range: shift supervisor, site supervisor, research supervisor.
normal.cn: 职位显示它的范围：值班主管、现场主管、研究导师。

normal.en: The vis- inside means seeing, which is why a supervisor is first an eye.
normal.cn: 其中的 vis- 意为看见，因此主管首先是一只眼。

normal.en: In computing the same name passed from the person to a program.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，同一个名称从人传给了程序。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that touches nothing but marks each finished piece with a stamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手什么也不碰，只给每件成品盖一个章。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp at the end of a tunnel that lights each worker as they pass.
abstract.cn: 想象隧道尽头的一盏灯，照着每个经过的工人。

abstract.en: Picture a list where every line is already ticked before the shift ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一张清单，班次结束前每行都已画了勾。

examples.en: Her supervisor signed off the report after one revision.
examples.cn: 她的导师在改过一稿后签批了报告。

examples.en: The shift supervisor sent two workers home early.
examples.cn: 值班主管让两名工人提前回家。

examples.en: A floor supervisor walks the aisles before the store opens.
examples.cn: 开店前，卖场主管会走一遍货架通道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「super（在上）+ visor（看的人）」——在上面看着的人，就是主管

root: 中世纪拉丁 supervisus（supervidere「巡视」的过去分词）+ 施动后缀；同根词有 supervise、supervision、vision。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one eye at work: it watches a crew, holds one shift, guides one student, sits on a county board, guards an exam, controls other programs, balances a hospital at night and protects a family visit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都让一只眼留在工作现场：看住工班、守住一个班次、带一个学生、坐在县政委员会、守住考场、控制其他程序、夜里平衡整座医院、保护一次家庭探视。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at the end of the line with a list, ticking each finished item.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人拿着清单站在产线末端，逐项打勾。

branches.en: THE CREW AND THE SHIFT: the same eye, once on the work and once on the clock.
branches.cn: 工班与班次：同一只眼，一次看活，一次看钟。

branches.en: THE STUDENT: the eye is lent to one person for years.
branches.cn: 学生：这只眼借给一个人好几年。

branches.en: THE COUNTY BOARD: local government borrows the title.
branches.cn: 县政委员会：地方政府借用了这个称号。

branches.en: THE GUARDED AND THE PROTECTED: an exam is watched to keep rules, a visit to keep people safe.
branches.cn: 看守与保护：监考为守规则，探视为保安全。

branches.en: THE MACHINE AND THE WARD: a program and a night officer both keep many parts in balance.
branches.cn: 机器与病区：一个程序与一位夜班主管都在让众多部分保持平衡。

intro.en: Supervisor is supervise plus an agent ending, and the seeing root behind it also builds words about sight and inspection.
intro.cn: supervisor 是 supervise 加上施动词尾，其背后的「看见」词根还构成与视觉、检查有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre gives vision, visible and evident; supervidere gives supervise, supervision and survey.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 videre 衍生 vision、visible 与 evident；supervidere 衍生 supervise、supervision 与 survey。

items.example: The prefix places the eye above the work.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把眼放在工作上方。

items.example: The compound is the medieval source.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是中世纪以来的源头。

items.example: The verb is the base of this noun.
items.exampleCN: 动词是这个名词的基座。

items.example: The action noun sits beside the person noun.
items.exampleCN: 动作名词与人名词并列。

items.example: The suffix names the office, not the person.
The cousin word keeps the same eye.
items.exampleCN: 这位表亲保留同一只眼。

definition_zh: 操作系统；管理计算机硬件与软件资源、为程序提供运行环境的系统软件
definition_en: the system software that manages a computer's hardware and software resources and provides services for programs
core_image: 一台刚开机的电脑屏幕上，语言、网络与账户三个选项依次排开，桌面还藏在后面
scene: 新买的电脑第一次开机，屏幕先让用户选语言、连网络，然后才进入桌面。 The operating system manages the memory that every program asks for.
sceneCN: 这里指管理硬件与软件资源的系统软件（第 1 个义项：管理计算机资源的系统软件）；句意为操作系统管理每个程序申请的内存。图中可辨识物件：开机画面、桌面图标、内存条、设置窗口。

pos.zh: 操作系统；系统软件

senses.title: The software that runs the machine
senses.definition: the system software that manages hardware, memory, files and processes and lets other programs run
senses.definitionCN: 管理硬件、内存、文件与进程、并让其他程序得以运行的系统软件
senses.example: The operating system manages the memory that every program asks for.
senses.exampleCN: 操作系统管理每个程序申请的内存。
senses.why: Operate names the running of a machine and system names an organised whole, so the phrase is the running whole.
senses.whyCN: 前一词命名机器的运行，后一词命名有组织的整体，因此这个短语就是「运行的整体」。

senses.title: A particular product
senses.definition: one named product that performs this role, sold in versions for different machines
senses.definitionCN: 执行这一角色的某个具名产品，按不同机器分版本出售
senses.example: The laptop ships with a different operating system.
senses.exampleCN: 这台笔记本预装了另一个操作系统。
senses.why: A common noun becomes a product name when several vendors sell their own version of the same role.
senses.whyCN: 当多家厂商各自出售同一角色的版本，普通名词就变成产品名。

senses.title: A mobile system
senses.definition: the system software of a phone or tablet, built for touch input and limited power
senses.definitionCN: 手机或平板的系统软件，为触控输入与有限电量而设计
senses.example: Most apps on the phone were written for its operating system.
senses.exampleCN: 手机上的多数应用是为它的操作系统写的。
senses.why: The same role moves to a smaller machine, and the phrase follows the device.
senses.whyCN: 同一角色搬到更小的机器，短语也跟着设备走。

senses.title: A server system
senses.definition: a system software build tuned for many users, long uptime and remote administration
senses.definitionCN: 为多用户、长时间运行与远程管理而调优的系统软件版本
senses.example: The server operating system was patched without a restart.
senses.exampleCN: 服务器操作系统在不重启的情况下打了补丁。
senses.why: The role stays the same, but the conditions of running change, so a separate branch appears.
senses.whyCN: 角色不变，运行条件变了，于是分出独立一支。

senses.title: An embedded or real-time system
senses.titleCN: 嵌入式或实时操作系统
senses.definition: a small system software build that must respond within fixed time limits, used inside devices
senses.definitionCN: 必须在固定时限内响应、装在设备内部的小型系统软件
senses.example: The car's operating system must react before the wheel turns.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车的操作系统必须在车轮转动前作出反应。
senses.why: When a machine cannot wait, the running whole is built to guarantee time, not to offer features.
senses.whyCN: 当机器不能等待，这个运行的整体就要保证时间，而不是提供功能。

senses.title: The platform for programs
senses.definition: the layer whose rules and services determine what other software can do
senses.definitionCN: 其规则与服务决定其他软件能做什么的那一层
senses.example: The game will not run on an older operating system.
senses.exampleCN: 这款游戏无法在较旧的操作系统上运行。
senses.why: Whoever controls the layer controls the ground on which other programs stand.
senses.whyCN: 谁控制这一层，谁就控制其他程序站立的地面。

senses.title: A layer in the stack
senses.definition: one layer between hardware and applications in a description of a computer's structure
senses.definitionCN: 在描述计算机结构时，位于硬件与应用之间的一层
senses.example: The diagram puts the operating system between the chip and the browser.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图把操作系统放在芯片与浏览器之间。
senses.why: The phrase can be abstracted into a layer, which is how computing textbooks use it.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以被抽象成一层，计算教材正是这样使用它。

senses.title: The legacy sense
senses.definition: the software that supervised jobs on early mainframes, the ancestor of the modern system
senses.definitionCN: 早期大型机上监督作业的软件，是现代系统的前身
senses.example: The museum keeps a tape from an early operating system.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆保存着一盘早期操作系统的磁带。
senses.why: The role existed before the phrase was fixed, and the older machines show the same running whole in plainer form.
senses.whyCN: 这个角色在短语固定之前就已存在，旧机器以更朴素的形式展示同一个运行整体。

intro.en: Operating system joins operating, from Latin operari 'to work', from opus 'work', and system, from Greek systema 'organised whole', from syn- 'together' and histanai 'to set up'. The phrase became standard in computing around 1960; the exact first use is source uncertain.
intro.cn: operating system 由 operating（拉丁 operari「工作」，源自 opus「工作」）与 system（希腊 systema「有组织的整体」，源自 syn-「一起」与 histanai「设立」）组合。该短语约一九六〇年在计算领域成为标准说法；最早用例来源不确定。

items.en: Latin opus meant work, especially a piece of work or a task, and it underlies operate, operation and opera.
items.cn: 拉丁 opus 指工作，尤指一件作品或一项任务，是 operate、operation 与 opera 的基底。

items.en: Operari meant to work or to be at work, and English operate kept the sense of a machine doing its work.
items.cn: operari 指工作或正在工作，英语 operate 保留「机器做它的活」这一义。

items.en: Greek systema meant an organised whole made of parts, from syn- 'together' and histanai 'to set up'.
items.cn: 希腊 systema 指由各部分组成的有组织整体，源自 syn-「一起」与 histanai「设立」。

items.en: English system kept the Greek sense of a whole of connected parts, and later applied it to bodies, laws and machines.
items.cn: 英语 system 保留希腊语「相互连接的部分构成的整体」之义，后来用于身体、法律与机器。

items.en: Around 1960 the phrase operating system was used for software that supervised jobs and resources; earlier machines used other names.
items.cn: 约一九六〇年，operating system 被用来指监督作业与资源的软件；更早的机器用别的名称。

items.en: Personal computers in the 1980s turned the phrase into product names, and mobile and embedded systems extended it further.
items.cn: 二十世纪八十年代的个人电脑把这个短语变成产品名，移动与嵌入式系统又把它推得更远。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like operating system; the second group names neighbouring ideas in the same field.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「operating system」相近；第二组是同一领域里意思相邻的其他说法。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to work or to control a machine.
entries.definitionCN: 指工作或操作机器的动词。

entries.definition: The act of running or a medical procedure, from the same work word.
entries.definitionCN: 运行行为或医疗手术，同出那个「工作」词。

entries.definition: A person who runs a machine, or a symbol that performs an action.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机器的人，或执行动作的符号。

entries.definition: In working order or ready for use, rather than related to an operating system.
entries.definitionCN: 处于可工作状态或可使用的，而非指操作系统。

entries.definition: An organised whole of parts, the second element of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 由各部分组成的有组织整体，短语的第二部分。

entries.definition: The core of a system that controls hardware and processes, smaller than the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 控制硬件与进程的系统核心，比整个系统更小。

entries.definition: Software fixed into a device that runs before a full system starts.
entries.definitionCN: 固定在设备中、在完整系统启动前运行的软件。

entries.definition: The layer or environment on which other software is built.
entries.definitionCN: 其他软件建立其上的层或环境。

entries.definition: The environment in which a program executes, narrower than a whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 程序执行的环境，比整个系统更窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin work word, the real Greek whole and real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实拉丁「工作」词、真实希腊「整体」词与真实技术搭配。

normal.en: Operate comes from Latin operari, to work, and system comes from Greek systema, an organised whole.
normal.cn: operate 来自拉丁 operari「工作」，system 来自希腊 systema「有组织的整体」。

normal.en: The phrase names the software whose work is to keep the whole machine working.
normal.cn: 这个短语命名的是「以维持整台机器运转为工作」的软件。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: mobile, desktop, server and real-time operating system.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各支：移动、桌面、服务器与实时操作系统。

normal.en: The abbreviation OS is used in shops and code alike.
normal.cn: 缩写 OS 在商店与代码里同样通用。

normal.en: A kernel is the core; the operating system is the whole arrangement around it.
normal.cn: 内核是核心，操作系统是围绕它的整套安排。

abstract.en: It is the floor on which every other program stands.
abstract.cn: 它是其他所有程序站立的地板。

abstract.en: When the floor shakes, every program feels it.
abstract.cn: 地板一晃，每个程序都感觉得到。

abstract.en: The user sees icons; the system sees resources being handed out.
abstract.cn: 用户看见图标，系统看见资源被分发。

examples.en: The update fixed a flaw in the operating system's memory handling.
examples.cn: 这次更新修复了操作系统内存管理中的一个漏洞。

examples.en: Without an operating system, every program would have to drive the hardware itself.
examples.cn: 没有操作系统，每个程序都得自己驱动硬件。

examples.en: The phone's operating system decides which app may use the camera.
examples.cn: 手机的操作系统决定哪个应用可以使用摄像头。

root: operating 来自拉丁 operari「工作」、opus「工作」；system 来自希腊 systema「有组织的整体」（syn- 一起 + histanai 设立）。短语约一九六〇年在计算领域通行，最早用例来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one running whole: the software that manages the machine, a product, a mobile build, a server build, an embedded build, a platform, a layer in a diagram, and its mainframe ancestor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个运行整体：管理机器的软件、一个产品、移动版本、服务器版本、嵌入式版本、一个平台、图中的一层，以及它的大型机前身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boot screen offering language, network and account, with the desktop still hidden behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：开机画面依次给出语言、网络与账户，桌面还藏在后面。

branches.en: THE RUNNING WHOLE: software does the work of keeping the machine and its programs running.
branches.cn: 运行的整体：软件承担维持机器与程序运转的工作。

branches.en: THE BUILDS: the same role is sold as products and tuned for phones, servers and devices that cannot wait.
branches.cn: 各种版本：同一角色既作为产品出售，也为手机、服务器与不能等待的设备调优。

branches.en: THE GROUND: whoever owns the layer decides what other programs may do.
branches.cn: 地面：谁拥有这一层，谁就决定其他程序能做什么。

branches.en: THE DIAGRAM LAYER: textbooks place it between the chip and the application.
branches.cn: 图中的一层：教材把它放在芯片与应用之间。

branches.en: THE ANCESTOR: early mainframes already had software supervising jobs, before the phrase was fixed.
branches.cn: 前身：早期大型机已有监督作业的软件，那时短语尚未固定。

intro.en: Operating system joins the Latin work word opus through operari with the Greek whole word systema.
intro.cn: operating system 把经 operari 而来的拉丁「工作」词 opus 与希腊「整体」词 systema 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin opus gives operari and English operate; Greek systema gives Latin systema and English system; English joins operating with system.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 opus 衍生 operari 与英语 operate；希腊 systema 衍生拉丁 systema 与英语 system；英语把 operating 与 system 连起来。

definition_en: the overall plan for how an experiment assigns treatments, controls conditions and collects observations
core_image: 一张试验田平面图，格子被分成不同处理区，中间留出对照行，播种顺序编成表
scene: 研究者先在纸上把试验田划分成若干区，标明哪些接受处理、哪些留作对照。 Poor experimental design can make a real effect disappear.
sceneCN: 这里指实验的整体安排（第 1 个义项：处理与对照的总体规划）；句意为糟糕的实验设计会让真实效应消失。

senses.title: The overall plan of an experiment
senses.definition: the complete arrangement of conditions, treatments and observations before data are collected
senses.definitionCN: 在收集数据之前对条件、处理与观测的完整安排
senses.example: A clear experimental design prevents wasted effort.
senses.exampleCN: 清楚的实验设计能避免白费力气。
senses.why: Design is a plan drawn in advance, and an experiment without one simply accumulates numbers.
senses.whyCN: 设计是事先画好的图，没有图的实验只是在堆积数字。

senses.title: Assignment of treatments and controls
senses.definition: the rule by which some units receive the treatment and others serve as comparison
senses.definitionCN: 规定哪些单位接受处理、哪些作为比较的规则
senses.example: The experimental design assigned half the plots to the new seed.
senses.exampleCN: 该实验设计把一半地块分给新种子。
senses.why: Comparison is the heart of an experiment, so assignment is the first thing the design must settle.
senses.whyCN: 比较是实验的核心，因此分配是设计首先要定下的事。

senses.title: Randomisation and replication
senses.definition: the structure that spreads chance evenly and repeats conditions enough to estimate error
senses.definitionCN: 把偶然均匀铺开、并重复条件以估计误差的结构
senses.example: Randomisation and replication are the backbone of the experimental design.
senses.exampleCN: 随机化与重复是实验设计的骨架。
senses.why: Chance and repetition do the work that intuition cannot: they make an effect visible against noise.
senses.whyCN: 偶然与重复做直觉做不到的事：让效应在噪声中显形。

senses.title: A between-subjects design
senses.definition: a plan in which different participants receive different conditions
senses.definitionCN: 不同参与者接受不同条件的方案
senses.example: The experimental design compared two separate groups.
senses.exampleCN: 该实验设计比较了两个独立的组。
senses.why: Separating people avoids practice effects but requires more participants, a real design trade-off.
senses.whyCN: 把人分开可避免练习效应，却需要更多参与者，这是实打实的设计权衡。

senses.title: A within-subjects design
senses.definition: a plan in which the same participants experience every condition
senses.definitionCN: 同一批参与者经历所有条件的方案
senses.example: A within-subjects experimental design reduces the number of volunteers needed.
senses.exampleCN: 组内实验设计减少了所需志愿者的数量。
senses.why: Using each person as their own comparison removes individual differences but invites order effects.
senses.whyCN: 让每个人做自己的比较能去掉个体差异，却会招来顺序效应。

senses.title: A factorial design
senses.definition: a plan that crosses two or more factors so that their separate and joint effects can be estimated
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多因素交叉组合，以估计各自与联合效应的方案
senses.example: The factorial experimental design crossed temperature with dose.
senses.exampleCN: 这个析因实验设计把温度与剂量交叉起来。
senses.why: Crossing factors turns a single study into several comparisons at once, which is why the design matters.
senses.whyCN: 交叉因素把一项研究同时变成几组比较，这正是设计的重要性。

senses.title: The protocol and its documentation
senses.definition: the written record of procedures, materials and decision rules that allows the study to be repeated
senses.definitionCN: 记录程序、材料与决策规则、使研究可被重复的书面文件
senses.example: The experimental design was registered before the first participant arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 实验设计在第一位参与者到来之前就已登记。
senses.why: A design that cannot be written down cannot be repeated, and an unrepeatable experiment is a story.
senses.whyCN: 写不下来的设计无法被重复，而不可重复的实验只是一个故事。

senses.title: A design chosen to avoid bias
senses.titleCN: 为避免偏差而选的设计
senses.definition: a plan whose structure removes known sources of systematic error such as selection or order effects
senses.definitionCN: 其结构能消除选择偏差、顺序效应等已知系统误差来源的方案
senses.example: Blinding was built into the experimental design to prevent bias.
senses.exampleCN: 实验设计中内置了盲法以防止偏差。
senses.why: Bias is a property of plans rather than of people, so it must be designed out in advance.
senses.whyCN: 偏差是方案的性质而非人的性质，因此必须在事先设计掉。

intro.en: Experimental design joins a Latin word for trial with a Latin verb for marking out. The trial supplies the testing, and the marking supplies the plan drawn before anything is done.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语中表示「尝试」的词，与表示「标出」的动词接在一起：尝试提供检验，标出提供动手之前画好的图。

items.en: Periri meant to try or attempt, and with the prefix for out it produced experiri, to test thoroughly.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「尝试」，加上表示「向外」的前缀后构成「彻底试」。

items.en: The noun named a trial or test, and English experiment came through French with the same core.
items.cn: 这个名词指试验或检验，英语的「实验」经法语而来，核心义相同。

items.en: The adjective appeared with the rise of natural philosophy, where knowledge was to be tested rather than argued.
items.cn: 这个形容词随自然哲学的兴起而出现，当时知识要靠检验而非论辩。

items.en: Signum meant a mark or sign, and designare meant to mark out and hence to plan.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「标记」，其动词意为标出，因而指规划。

items.en: Design entered through French and Italian for a plan or a drawing, before it meant the arrangement of a study.
items.cn: 这个词经法语与意大利语进入英语，先指平面图或图样，后指研究的安排。

items.en: Statistical texts fixed experimental design as the branch that plans comparisons; the exact first record of the phrase is uncertain.
items.cn: 统计学教材把「实验设计」固定为规划比较的分支；该短语确切最早记录不确定。

note.en: The first group belongs to the experiment family; the second group names neighbouring plans and methods.
note.cn: 第一组属于「实验」同族；第二组指相邻的规划与方法。

entries.definition: A test carried out to see what happens under stated conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 指在规定条件下进行、观察结果的检验。

entries.definition: Relating to or based on experiments.
entries.definitionCN: 指与实验有关的或以实验为基础的。

entries.definition: By means of an experiment.
entries.definitionCN: 指以实验方式。

entries.definition: The activity of running experiments.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事实验的活动。

entries.definition: The person who runs an experiment.
entries.definitionCN: 指做实验的人。

entries.definition: A plan or pattern made in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 指事先制定的方案或图样。

entries.definition: The broader plan of a study, including sampling and measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指更宽的研究规划，含抽样与测量。

entries.definition: The written procedure that the design is turned into.
entries.definitionCN: 指设计转化成的书面程序。

entries.definition: The principles behind the choice of methods, broader than one design.
entries.definitionCN: 指方法选择背后的原则，比单个设计更宽。

entries.definition: A plan with comparison groups but without random assignment.
entries.definitionCN: 指有对照组但无随机分配的方案。

entries.definition: The rule for choosing which units enter the study.
entries.definitionCN: 指选择哪些单位进入研究的规则。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the plot map, randomisation and replication, and the trade-offs between designs.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用地块平面图、随机化与重复，以及不同设计之间的权衡。

normal.en: Design is a mark made in advance, so experimental design is the map drawn before the first measurement.
normal.cn: 设计是事先做的标记，所以实验设计是第一次测量之前画好的图。

normal.en: The fixed textbook phrase is «experimental design and analysis», pairing the plan with its statistics.
normal.cn: 教材里的固定说法是「实验设计与分析」，把规划与统计配在一起。

normal.en: Between-subjects needs more people; within-subjects needs fewer but risks order effects.
normal.cn: 组间设计需要更多人，组内设计需要人少却有顺序效应之险。

normal.en: Randomisation and replication are the two pillars under every sound experimental design.
normal.cn: 随机化与重复是每个可靠实验设计下的两根柱子。

normal.en: Blinding is designed in, because bias belongs to the plan and not to the person.
normal.cn: 盲法是设计进去的，因为偏差属于方案而不属于个人。

abstract.en: A design is the argument made before the data can speak.
abstract.cn: 设计是数据开口之前就已作出的论证。

abstract.en: An experiment without a plan is only a busy room.
abstract.cn: 没有方案的实验只是一间忙碌的屋子。

abstract.en: The strongest designs make it possible to be wrong, and that possibility is what makes them trustworthy.
abstract.cn: 最强的设计让「被证明错了」成为可能，正是这种可能使它可信。

examples.en: The experimental design used four groups with two crossed factors.
examples.cn: 该实验设计使用了四个组与两个交叉因素。

examples.en: Flaws in the experimental design made the results impossible to interpret.
examples.cn: 实验设计的缺陷使结果无法解释。

examples.en: She revised the experimental design after the pilot study.
examples.cn: 预试验之后她修改了实验设计。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「实验」是去试，「设计」是先画：试之前把地块、处理与对照都画在图上，就是实验设计

root: 「实验」来自拉丁语 experimentum「试验」，其动词 experiri 意为「彻底试」，由 ex-「向外」与表示「尝试」的词根构成；「设计」来自拉丁语 designare「标出」，由 de- 与 signum「标记」构成。统计学教材把「实验设计」固定为规划比较的分支；该短语最早记录不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the whole plan to its safeguards: the overall arrangement, treatment assignment, randomisation and replication, between-subjects, within-subjects, factorial crossing, written protocol, and bias prevention.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整体规划延伸到防偏措施：总体安排、处理分配、随机化与重复、组间设计、组内设计、析因交叉、书面方案、防偏设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field is marked into plots on paper, with treated rows and a control row laid out before planting.
core.cn: 核心意象：田地在纸上被划成小区，处理行与对照行在播种之前就已排好。

branches.en: THE DRAWN PLAN: the complete arrangement, its written protocol and its repeatability.
branches.cn: 画好的图：完整安排、书面方案与可重复性。

branches.en: THE ASSIGNMENT RULE: who receives the treatment and who serves as comparison.
branches.cn: 分配规则：谁接受处理，谁作为比较。

branches.en: THE TWO PILLARS: chance spread evenly and conditions repeated.
branches.cn: 两根柱子：偶然被均匀铺开，条件被重复。

branches.en: THE TWO COMPARISONS: different people across groups, or the same people across conditions.
branches.cn: 两种比较：不同人跨组，或同一人跨条件。

branches.en: THE CROSSED AND GUARDED: factors crossed to reveal joint effects, and structure built against bias.
branches.cn: 交叉与防护：交叉因素显出联合效应，结构用来抵御偏差。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin trial word to a Latin marking word, so an experiment is a test and a design is a plan drawn beforehand.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语的「尝试」与「标记」接起来：实验是检验，设计是事先画好的图。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies experiri and designare; the statistical sense of the compound is modern and its first record is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「彻底试」与「标出」；该复合词的统计义属现代用法，最早记录不确定。

definition_zh: 山坡；斜坡（苏格兰用语）
definition_en: a slope or hillside, a Scottish word
core_image: 苏格兰高地上一条斜斜的草坡，羊群散落在坡腰，小路蜿蜒而上
scene: 老牧人指着村子后头说家就在那儿。 Their cottage stood halfway up the brae, with a view of the whole glen.
sceneCN: 这里 brae 是「山坡」（第 1 个义项：斜坡地形）；句意是他们的农舍坐落在半山腰，可以俯瞰整个峡谷。

pos.zh: 山坡；斜坡

derivatives.zh: 由复合词构成，义为「坡边地带」
由复合词构成，义为「坡地」

senses.title: A slope or hillside
senses.definition: a stretch of rising ground, especially a grassy hillside
senses.definitionCN: 一段地势升高的地面，尤指长草的山坡
senses.example: Sheep grazed all over the brae.
senses.exampleCN: 羊群在山坡上四处吃草。
senses.why: The Old Norse word for eyelid or brow gave the picture of land's brow rising like a lid.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语中指「眉、睑」的词给出画面：大地如眼睑般隆起的边沿即坡。

senses.title: A road or path going uphill
senses.definition: a sloping street or track, especially in Scottish towns
senses.definitionCN: 倾斜的街道或小径，常见于苏格兰城镇
senses.example: The cart labored up the brae toward the market.
senses.exampleCN: 马车吃力地爬坡驶向市场。
senses.why: The land form names the way built upon it, as hill gave hill road.
senses.whyCN: 地形名转指建于其上的道路，如 hill 之有 hill road。

senses.title: A slope as boundary of a settlement
senses.definition: the hillside at the edge of a village or field
senses.definitionCN: 村庄或田地边缘的山坡
senses.example: The cottages lined the foot of the brae.
senses.exampleCN: 农舍沿坡脚一字排开。
senses.why: Human settlement clings to slopes; the word marks where the flat land ends.
senses.whyCN: 人类聚落依坡而建，这个词标记平地的尽头。

senses.title: Steady effort, as in climbing
senses.definition: in phrases, the strain of going uphill, literal or figurative
senses.definitionCN: 在短语中指上坡的吃力，实指或比喻
senses.example: Getting the budget approved was a long pull up the brae.
senses.exampleCN: 预算获批如爬长坡，一步一吃力。
senses.why: Climbing a slope is the plainest image of hard gradual progress.
senses.whyCN: 爬坡是「渐进的艰辛」最直白的意象。

senses.title: A viewpoint on rising ground
senses.definition: a spot on the slope from which the land below is seen
senses.definitionCN: 坡上可俯瞰下方的位置
senses.example: From the brae we watched the ships come in.
senses.exampleCN: 我们从坡上望着船只进港。
senses.why: Height is for seeing; the slope becomes a stand for the eye.
senses.whyCN: 高处的功能是看，坡便成了眼睛的看台。

senses.title: Home ground in rural speech
senses.definition: the local hillside as the beloved home landscape in Scots writing
senses.definitionCN: 苏格兰文学中作为故乡风物的本地山坡
senses.example: The poet sang of the braes of his boyhood.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人歌咏自己少年时代的家山。
senses.why: Everyday landscape words turn tender in rural poetry.
senses.whyCN: 日常地貌词在乡土诗歌中染上温情。

senses.title: An incline measured by work
senses.definition: the degree of slope judged by how hard it is to climb or haul
senses.definitionCN: 以攀爬或拉运之难易判断的坡度
senses.example: That brae is too steep for a loaded cart.
senses.exampleCN: 那道坡太陡，满载的马车过不去。
senses.why: Farmers grade land not by degrees but by the sweat it costs.
senses.whyCN: 农人不用度数而用汗水丈量坡度。

senses.title: A place-name element
senses.definition: brae as a common element in Scottish place names
senses.definitionCN: brae 作为苏格兰地名的常见成分
senses.example: Many villages carry the word brae in their names.
senses.exampleCN: 许多村庄的名字里都带着 brae 一词。
senses.why: Long use fixes the land word into the map itself.
senses.whyCN: 长年使用使地貌词固化进了地图。

intro.en: Brae is a Northern English and Scots word borrowed from Old Norse, where it meant brow or eyelid.
intro.cn: brae 是北部英语与苏格兰语用词，借自古诺斯语，原义为「眉、睑」。

items.en: A reconstructed root *brāwō meant brow or edge, shared across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 重构词根 *brāwō 意为「眉、边沿」，见于各日耳曼语言。

items.en: Old Norse brá meant eyelid or brow, the image of the land's rising edge.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 brá 意为「睑、眉」，引申出大地隆起的边沿之象。

items.en: Settlers of Norse descent carried brá into northern England and Scotland as brae, meaning slope.
items.cn: 诺斯裔移民把 brá 带进英格兰北部和苏格兰，作 brae，意为山坡。

items.en: Scots writing shows brae freely for hillside and sloping road.
items.cn: 十五至十六世纪苏格兰文献中，brae 已通用于山坡与坡路。

items.en: Robert Burns's dialect poems fixed the word in the literary imagination.
items.cn: 彭斯的方言诗使这个词定格于文学想象之中。

items.en: Modern use is regional and literary; standard English keeps slope or hillside.
items.cn: 现代用法具地域与文学色彩；标准英语通用 slope 或 hillside。

note.en: Brae is short and regional; its look-alikes are common words that merely share sounds.
note.cn: brae 短小且具地域性；形近词只是同音的常见词。

entries.definition: the loud cry of a donkey
entries.definitionCN: 驴叫声；与 brae 同音，词源不同

entries.definition: the forehead, or the top edge of a hill
entries.definitionCN: 额头；坡顶；同源英语形式

entries.definition: a device for stopping; a fern
entries.definitionCN: 刹车；蕨草；拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a pair, or to support
entries.definitionCN: 一对；支撑；拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to cook slowly in a covered pot
entries.definitionCN: 炖；焖；拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a surface rising or falling at an angle
entries.definitionCN: 斜面；坡；通用词

entries.definition: the sloping side of a hill
entries.definitionCN: 山坡；与 brae 最接近的标准英语对应

entries.definition: a slope, often a road or rail gradient
entries.definitionCN: 斜坡；常指道路坡度

entries.definition: a slope of earth beside a river or road
entries.definitionCN: 土坡；河岸坡

entries.definition: the degree of slope of a road
entries.definitionCN: 坡度；（美）斜坡路段

normalIntro.en: Tie brae to brow: the hill's brow is the brae.
normalIntro.cn: 把 brae 与 brow 联系起来：山的「眉额」就是坡。

normal.en: brae comes from Old Norse brá, eyelid or brow.
normal.cn: brae 源自古诺斯语 brá，意为睑、眉。

normal.en: brow is the native English cousin, same root.
normal.cn: brow 是英语本土同源词。

normal.en: it survives in Scottish place names like Auchendinny Brae.
normal.cn: 它保存在诸如 Auchendinny Brae 这样的苏格兰地名里。

normal.en: Burns wrote of the braes of youth.
normal.cn: 彭斯写过少年时代的 braes。

normal.en: the plural braes is common in poetry.
normal.cn: 复数 braes 在诗歌中常见。

abstract.en: See the land tilt like a raised eyelid.
abstract.cn: 把大地想象成掀起的眼睑。

abstract.en: Sheep dots on green are the word's fixed picture.
abstract.cn: 绿坡上的羊点是这个词的固定画面。

abstract.en: Every uphill street in an old Scottish town is a brae.
abstract.cn: 苏格兰老城里每条上坡街都是一条 brae。

examples.en: They built their cottage on the sunny side of the brae.
examples.cn: 他们把农舍建在山坡向阳的一侧。

examples.en: The old cart track wound up the brae behind the kirk.
examples.cn: 老旧的车辙小路蜿蜒爬上教堂后的山坡。

examples.en: From the top of the brae, the whole valley lay below like a map.
examples.cn: 从坡顶望下去，整个山谷如地图般铺展。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不累」——走平地不累，一上「不累」就想歇：brae 就是那道让人半途歇脚的坡。

root: 日耳曼语系重构词根 *brāwō（眉、边沿）→ 古诺斯语 brá（睑、眉）→ 苏格兰语 brae（山坡）；与英语本土词 brow 同源。

sensesIntro.en: From the landform itself, the word spreads to the road on it, the home ground beside it, and the effort and view it affords.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项由坡体本身出发，延伸至坡上之路、坡畔人家，以及坡带来的费力与视野。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the land's brow, a green slope tilting up from the flat
core.cn: 核心意象：大地的眉额——一块从平地翘起的绿坡

branches.en: the form: grass rising at an angle
branches.cn: 形体：斜斜升起的草坡

branches.en: the way: roads graded by the pull of the climb
branches.cn: 道路：以攀拉之力度量坡度

branches.en: the home: cottages and poems at the slope's edge
branches.cn: 家园：坡畔的农舍与诗篇

branches.en: the strain: progress measured in uphill pulls
branches.cn: 吃力：以爬坡计量的进展

branches.en: the eye and the map: a viewpoint, a name on the land
branches.cn: 眼与地图：观景处与地名

intro.en: Brae is a single morpheme from Norse; compounds are made by simple juxtaposition.
intro.cn: brae 是来自诺斯语的单语素词；复合词由简单并置构成。

latinIntro.en: The Germanic family of *brāwō has no Latin relatives; Latin supercilium covers the same brow idea.
latinIntro.cn: *brāwō 的日耳曼词族在拉丁语中无亲属；拉丁语 supercilium 表达同样的「眉额」概念。

诺斯语 brá 演变为苏格兰语 brae

items.example: eyebrow keeps the old sense alive
brae-side is the land along the slope
hill is the standard word brae narrows
