glen 位于 brae 之下

definition_zh: 惯常的；按习俗的；法律上以惯例为依据的
definition_en: usual because it is established by custom, and in law based on long-standing practice rather than statute
core_image: 村口的路上，来往的人见到长辈都会停下来说一句话
scene: 村口的路上，来往的人见到长辈都会停下来说一句话。 It is customary to remove your shoes before entering the shrine.
sceneCN: 这里 customary 指「按习俗的、惯常的」（第 1 个义项：因长期惯例而成为通常做法）；句意为进神龛前脱鞋是惯常的礼俗。可辨识物件：村口、神龛、鞋、石阶。

pos.zh: 惯常的；按习俗的；习惯法上的

senses.title: Usual because custom requires it
senses.titleCN: 因习俗而成为通常做法的
senses.definition: describing what people normally do because long practice expects it
senses.definitionCN: 描述人们因长期惯例的期待而通常做的事
senses.example: It is customary to remove your shoes before entering the shrine.
senses.exampleCN: 进神龛前脱鞋是惯常的礼俗。
senses.why: custom plus -ary means 'according to custom', so the adjective reports an expectation rather than a law.
senses.whyCN: custom 加 -ary 意为「按习俗的」，因此这个形容词报告一种期待，而非法律。

senses.title: Expected in a social exchange
senses.definition: describing the greeting, gift or thanks that a situation calls for
senses.definitionCN: 描述某场合所要求的问候、礼物或致谢
senses.example: A customary bow followed the introduction.
senses.exampleCN: 介绍之后行了一个惯常的鞠躬礼。
senses.why: social life runs on small expectations, and the word marks them as normal.
senses.whyCN: 社会生活靠细小的期待运转，这个词把它们标记为正常。

senses.title: Based on practice in law
senses.titleCN: 法律上以惯例为依据的
senses.definition: describing rights or rules that courts recognize because they have long been practised
senses.definitionCN: 描述法院因长期实践而承认的权利或规则
senses.example: Customary rights to the fishing ground predate the statute.
senses.exampleCN: 对渔场的习惯权利早于成文法存在。
senses.why: before written law, practice was law, and the adjective preserves that authority.
senses.whyCN: 在成文法之前，实践就是法律，这个形容词保留了那份权威。

senses.title: Recognized in international law
senses.definition: describing rules that states follow consistently and treat as legally binding
senses.definitionCN: 描述各国一贯遵循并视为有法律约束力的规则
senses.example: Customary international law binds states that never signed the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 习惯国际法约束那些从未签署条约的国家。
senses.why: international law borrowed the idea that repeated conduct can create an obligation.
senses.whyCN: 国际法借用了「反复行为可以产生义务」这一观念。

senses.title: Ordinary or average
senses.definition: used of a normal amount of time or effort, without any ritual weight
senses.definitionCN: 指通常的时间或努力程度，不带仪式分量
senses.example: The repair took the customary two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修花了通常的两小时。
senses.why: the word can weaken into 'as usual', once the habit is no longer noticed.
senses.whyCN: 当习惯不再被注意，这个词就可弱化为「照常」。

senses.title: Belonging to a traditional rite
senses.definition: describing the acts that a local ceremony normally includes
senses.definitionCN: 描述地方仪式通常包含的动作
senses.example: The customary offering is rice, salt and clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 惯常的供品是米、盐与清水。
senses.why: rites are the place where custom is most strictly expected.
senses.whyCN: 仪式是习俗被要求得最严格的地方。

senses.title: Socially expected of a person
senses.definition: describing behaviour that others assume a person in a role will show
senses.definitionCN: 描述他人假定某一角色者会表现出的行为
senses.example: It was customary for the host to walk guests to the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 主人送客到门口是惯常的做法。
senses.why: a role carries expectations, and the adjective names them without making them rules.
senses.whyCN: 角色自带期待，这个形容词指出这些期待，却不把它们变成规则。

senses.title: The quality of being conventional
senses.definition: the state of being usual by custom, used in legal and social description
senses.definitionCN: 因习俗而成为通常状态的性质，用于法律与社会描述
senses.example: Lawyers debated the customariness of the old route.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们争论这条古道的惯常性。
senses.why: once a practice is disputed, its quality of being customary must itself be argued.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某种做法有争议，它「是否属于惯例」这一性质本身就要被论证。

intro.en: Customary comes from Medieval Latin consuetudinarius 'according to custom', from consuetudo 'habit', and reached English through Old French coutumier. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: customary 来自中世纪拉丁 consuetudinarius「按习俗的」，出自 consuetudo「习惯」，经古法语 coutumier 进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Consuetudo meant 'habit, usage, customary right', built on consuescere 'to accustom'. Its deeper root suescere 'become used' is of uncertain origin.
items.cn: consuetudo 意为「习惯、惯例、习惯法权利」，由 consuescere「使习惯」构成。其更深词根 suescere「变得习惯」来源不确定。

items.en: The suffix -arius formed adjectives and nouns of belonging, giving consuetudinarius 'according to custom'.
items.cn: 后缀 -arius 构成表归属的形容词与名词，于是有 consuetudinarius「按习俗的」。

items.en: Old French coutumier carried the adjective into English, where it described local rules and personal habits alike.
items.cn: 古法语 coutumier 把这个形容词带入英语，既描述地方规则，也描述个人习惯。

items.en: English courts used customary for rights proved by long practice, as opposed to rights granted by statute.
items.cn: 英国法院用 customary 指由长期实践证明的权利，与成文法授予的权利相对。

items.en: Modern international law extended the word to rules formed by consistent state conduct.
items.cn: 现代国际法把这个词扩展到由各国一贯行为形成的规则。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest legal uses of the English adjective are dated only approximately, and the pre-Latin origin of suescere is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个英语形容词最早的法学用法只有约略年代；suescere 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike forms of the same root; group two holds near synonyms for what is normally done.
note.cn: 第一组是同根的形近形式；第二组是表示「通常如此」的近义词。

entries.definition: The practice itself; customary is the adjective saying something follows it.
entries.definitionCN: 指做法本身；customary 是说明某事物遵循它的形容词。

entries.definition: A habitual buyer, from the same root in its sense of habitual use; it has nothing to do with rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指习惯性买家，同根但取「习惯性使用」义，与规则无关。

entries.definition: The same Old French source, now meaning clothing rather than practice.
entries.definitionCN: 同一古法语来源，今指服装而非做法。

entries.definition: Means 'as is usual', used to soften a statement about normal practice.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「按照惯例」，用来缓和关于通常做法的陈述。

entries.definition: Happening most often, with no reference to custom or law.
entries.definitionCN: 指最常发生，不涉及习俗或法律。

entries.definition: Following accepted social style, often in a slightly critical tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指遵循被接受的社会风格，常带轻微批评口吻。

entries.definition: Describing a repeated personal behaviour, often hard to break.
entries.definitionCN: 描述个人反复的行为，常难以改掉。

entries.definition: Conforming to what is expected in general; customary is narrower and ties expectation to tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 指符合一般期待；customary 更窄，把期待绑在传统上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: consuetudo 'habit' plus -arius 'belonging to' gives 'belonging to habit', then 'according to custom'.
normal.cn: consuetudo「习惯」加 -arius「属于……的」，先得「属于习惯的」，再得「按习俗的」。

normal.en: The family runs custom, customary, customarily, customariness and customer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 custom、customary、customarily、customariness 与 customer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: customary practice, customary law, customary rights, as is customary.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：惯常做法、习惯法、习惯上的权利、按照惯例。

normal.en: Customary law is law proved by long practice, not by a written statute.
normal.cn: 习惯法是由长期实践证明的法律，而非成文法规。

normal.en: The adverb customarily usually means 'as people normally do', not 'as the law requires'.
normal.cn: 副词 customarily 通常意为「人们通常这样做」，而非「法律要求这样」。

abstract.en: Picture a greeting performed before anyone decides to perform it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问候，在任何人决定做它之前就已经被做了。

abstract.en: Picture a rule with no book, only many mornings.
abstract.cn: 想象一条没有书本、只有许多个早晨的规则。

abstract.en: Picture a road that became official only because everyone kept walking it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路，只因所有人一直走，才成了正式的路。

examples.en: It is customary to bring the host a small gift.
examples.cn: 给主人带一份小礼物是惯常做法。

examples.en: Customary law still governs land in many rural districts.
examples.cn: 在许多乡村地区，土地仍由习惯法管辖。

examples.en: The ceremony followed its customary order without a single change.
examples.cn: 典礼按惯常顺序进行，毫无改动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「custom（习俗）+ ary（……的）」——按老规矩来的

root: 中世纪拉丁 consuetudinarius「按习俗的」，出自拉丁 consuetudo「习惯、惯例」，后者由 con- + suescere 构成；经古法语 coutumier 进入英语。suescere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one expectation: a practice is treated as normal, and that normality is then read as social courtesy, legal right, international rule, mere averageness, ritual form and disputed customariness.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个期待展开：一种做法被视为正常，这种正常再依次被读作社交礼节、法律权利、国际规则、平常程度、仪式形式与有争议的惯常性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a greeting performed before anyone decides to perform it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个问候，在任何人决定做它之前就已经被做了。

branches.en: THE BASE: what people normally do because long practice expects it.
branches.cn: 基础：人们因长期惯例的期待而通常做的事。

branches.en: COURTESY AND RITE: a bow and an offering are the same expectation in different settings.
branches.cn: 礼节与仪式：鞠躬与献供是同一期待在不同场合的表现。

branches.en: FROM COURT TO TREATY: practice becomes a right, and consistent conduct becomes binding law.
branches.cn: 从法庭到条约：实践变成权利，一贯行为变成有约束力的法律。

branches.en: THE ROLE: others assume a person will behave as the position expects.
branches.cn: 角色：他人假定某人会按这个位置所期待的方式行事。

branches.en: THE FADED AND THE DISPUTED: habit can weaken into 'ordinary', or become a quality that must be argued in court.
branches.cn: 淡化与争议：习惯可弱化为「平常」，也可变成必须在法庭上论证的性质。

intro.en: Customary adds a Latin relational suffix to the Latin noun of habit, and English later added -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: customary 在拉丁「习惯」名词上加了拉丁关系后缀，英语后来又加 -ly 与 -ness。

latinIntro.en: Consuetudo supplied the stem and -arius the relational ending; Old French reshaped it into coutumier before English borrowed the word.
latinIntro.cn: consuetudo 提供词干，-arius 提供关系词尾；古法语先把它改写为 coutumier，英语再借入。

items.example: The stem names the practice behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干指形容词背后的做法。

items.example: The suffix makes a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.example: Medieval lawyers used it of local rules.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪法学家用它指地方规则。

items.example: French shortened the long Latin ending.
items.exampleCN: 法语缩短了冗长的拉丁词尾。

items.example: English kept the legal and everyday senses together.
items.exampleCN: 英语把法律义与日常义保留在一起。

items.example: Customarily means in the customary way.
Customariness is the quality of being customary.
items.exampleCN: customariness 是「属于惯例」的性质。

items.example: The noun is the base of the adjective.
The -er form points at a person, not a rule.

definition_zh: 受益人；受惠者；（遗嘱、保险、信托等的）受益方
definition_en: a person or organization that receives money or an advantage under a will, policy, trust, or other arrangement
core_image: 一份文件的受益人栏上写着一个名字，箭头从文件指向这个人
scene: 她把人寿保单的受益人一栏填上妹妹的名字。 She named her sister as the sole beneficiary of her life insurance policy.
sceneCN: 这里 beneficiary 是「受益人」（第 2 个义项：保险金受益人）；句意：她指定妹妹作为她人寿保险的唯一受益人。场景要点：保单、受益人栏、签名、保险公司印章、信封。

pos.zh: 受益人；受惠者；（保险、遗嘱、信托的）受益方

senses.title: One named in a will
senses.titleCN: 遗嘱受益人：按遗嘱取得财产的人
senses.definition: a person named in a will to receive property or money from an estate
senses.definitionCN: 在遗嘱中被指定从遗产中获得财产或钱财的人
senses.example: Her three grandchildren were the beneficiaries of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 她的三个孙辈是这笔遗产的受益人。
senses.why: beneficium is a favor or benefit, and -arius names the person connected with it; English -ary carries that personal sense. The first English use (1610s) was simply 'one who receives profits or advantages', and a will is the oldest concrete setting for that idea.
senses.whyCN: beneficium 是恩惠或好处，-arius 指与之相关的人，英语 -ary 承接了这个指人的含义。该词 1610 年代最早只是“获得利润或好处的人”，而遗嘱是这一观念最古老的落地场景。

senses.title: Insurance beneficiary
senses.titleCN: 保险金受益人：保单指定领钱的人
senses.definition: the person or party named in an insurance policy to receive its payout
senses.definitionCN: 在保险单中被指定领取保险金的人或方
senses.example: The policy pays the beneficiary directly, outside the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 保单直接向受益人赔付，不进入遗产程序。
senses.why: Insurance law lets a nomination do the work: the named person steps into the benefit at death. The general 'receiver of advantage' is narrowed to a named payee, which is why a beneficiary need not be an heir.
senses.whyCN: 保险法让“指定”本身发挥作用：被指定者在被保险人死亡时直接承接这笔利益。泛指的“好处接受者”在这里收窄为具名收款人，所以受益人未必是继承人。

senses.title: Trust beneficiary
senses.titleCN: 信托受益人：享有信托利益的人
senses.definition: a person entitled to income or capital from a trust, while a trustee holds the legal title
senses.definitionCN: 有权从信托中获得收益或本金、而由受托人持有法定所有权的人
senses.example: The trust's beneficiaries receive the income but do not control the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 信托受益人领取收益，但不控制本金。
senses.why: In a trust, legal title and enjoyment split: the trustee holds, the beneficiary enjoys. The word names the equitable side of that split, which is the same 'one who enjoys the benefit' idea in technical form.
senses.whyCN: 在信托中，法定所有权与享受权被拆开：受托人持有，受益人享有。这个词命名的正是这条裂缝中“享有”的那一侧，也就是“享有利益者”这一观念的技术形态。

senses.title: Charity or aid recipient
senses.definition: a person or household that receives help from a charity, welfare scheme, or aid programme
senses.definitionCN: 从慈善机构、福利计划或援助项目获得帮助的个人或家庭
senses.example: The programme asks each beneficiary to attend a training session.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目要求每位受助者参加一次培训。
senses.why: Aid language prefers beneficiary to 'poor person' because it frames the person as the rightful receiver of a benefit, not as an object of pity. The legal word supplies dignity as well as precision.
senses.whyCN: 援助话语更愿意用 beneficiary 而不是“穷人”，因为它把人框定为“有资格获得好处的人”，而不是被怜悯的对象。这个法律词同时提供了精确与尊严。

senses.title: Payment beneficiary in banking
senses.titleCN: 银行付款的收款人；信用证受益人
senses.definition: the party to whom a payment is to be made, especially under a transfer or letter of credit
senses.definitionCN: 应收款的一方，尤指汇款或信用证项下的收款人
senses.example: The bank released the funds once the beneficiary presented the shipping documents.
senses.exampleCN: 受益人一提交装运单据，银行就放款了。
senses.why: In banking the benefit is a payment, so the beneficiary is the party to whom money is owed or addressed. The word becomes a technical label printed on forms, and the 'benefit' is reduced to a sum of money.
senses.whyCN: 在银行业务中，好处就是一笔付款，所以 beneficiary 是应收款或被指定收款的一方。这个词成了印在单据上的技术标签，“好处”被压缩为一笔金额。

senses.title: Third-party beneficiary of a contract
senses.definition: a person outside a contract who is intended to receive its benefit and may enforce it
senses.definitionCN: 合同之外、被意图给予合同利益并可据此主张权利的人
senses.example: The subcontractor was a third-party beneficiary of the main contract.
senses.exampleCN: 分包商是主合同的第三方受益人。
senses.why: Contract law extends the will model: a person who never signed the agreement may still be its intended receiver. Beneficiary then means 'the one the promise was meant to benefit', not 'the one who made the promise'.
senses.whyCN: 合同法延伸了遗嘱模型：从未签过协议的人也可能是约定的受益对象。此时 beneficiary 指“承诺本想使之受益的人”，而不是“作出承诺的人”。

senses.title: Development beneficiary or country
senses.titleCN: 发展项目的受益群体；受援国
senses.definition: a community, household group, or country that receives development assistance
senses.definitionCN: 接受发展援助的社区、家庭群体或国家
senses.example: The report compared outcomes across five beneficiary countries.
senses.exampleCN: 报告比较了五个受援国的结果。
senses.why: When the receiver is a whole community or state, the noun becomes a policy category. The benefit is now development assistance rather than a private gift, so the word works at the scale of projects and governments.
senses.whyCN: 当接受方是整个社区或国家时，这个名词变成政策类别。此时的好处是发展援助而非私人赠与，于是这个词在项目与政府的尺度上运作。

senses.title: Anyone who gains from an event
senses.titleCN: 泛指受益者：从某事中得到好处的人
senses.definition: a person or group that profits from a change, event, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 从某种变化、事件或局势中获利的人或群体
senses.example: Small exporters were the main beneficiaries of the weaker currency.
senses.exampleCN: 小出口商是货币走弱的主要受益者。
senses.why: Once the legal senses are established, the word can be used loosely of anyone who profits from an event. The benefit need not come from a document at all; it can come from a policy, a storm, or a market move.
senses.whyCN: 法律义项确立之后，这个词可以宽松地指任何从事件中获利的人。好处完全不必来自文件，也可以来自政策、风暴或市场波动。

senses.title: Attributive: the receiving side
senses.titleCN: 受益方的：作定语指接受的一方
senses.definition: used before another noun to label the receiving side of a scheme or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 置于另一名词前，标记某项计划或安排中接受的一方的
senses.example: Beneficiary families received the cash transfer at the start of each term.
senses.exampleCN: 受益家庭在每学期开始时收到现金补助。
senses.why: English often puts a noun before another noun instead of using an adjective, and beneficiary does this job in phrases such as beneficiary country and beneficiary family. It still names a person or party, but it now modifies rather than stands alone.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用名词而非形容词来修饰另一个名词，beneficiary 就在 beneficiary country、beneficiary family 这类短语里承担这个功能。它仍然指人或一方，但此时是修饰而非独立充当名词。

intro.en: Beneficiary and beneficial come from the same Latin noun beneficium, but they are not the same derivative. Beneficial goes through the adjective suffix -alis and names a quality; beneficiary goes through -arius and names a person. The noun reached English in the 1610s, probably through French.
intro.cn: beneficiary 和 beneficial 出自同一个拉丁名词 beneficium，但它们不是同一条派生。beneficial 走 -alis 这一形容词后缀，命名性质；beneficiary 走 -arius，命名人。这个名词在 17 世纪 10 年代进入英语，可能经由法语。

items.en: bene 'well' plus facere 'to do, make' produce beneficus 'generous, kind, obliging', literally 'doing well'. The pair is the common base of benefit, benefactor, beneficial and beneficiary.
items.cn: bene“好”加上 facere“做、造”产生 beneficus“慷慨的、善良的、乐于助人的”，字面即“做好事”。这一对成分是 benefit、benefactor、beneficial、beneficiary 的共同基础。

items.en: The noun beneficium 'a favor, service, kindness' adds -ium to the stem. It can mean a concrete benefit, a kindness done, and later a church office granted as a 'benefit' with its income.
items.cn: 名词 beneficium“恩惠、服务、善意”在词干上加 -ium。它可以指具体的好处、一次善举，后来也指作为“好处”授予的、带收入的教会圣职。

items.en: beneficiarius means 'enjoying a favor, privileged', built with -arius 'connected with, belonging to'. In Latin it describes a person attached to a benefit; the suffix is personal, not abstract.
items.cn: beneficiarius 意为“享有恩惠的、有特权的”，由 -arius“与……有关的、属于……的”构成。在拉丁语中它描述与好处相连的人；这个后缀是指人的，不是抽象性质的。

items.en: English beneficiary (1610s) probably came via French bénéficiaire, first as a noun 'one who receives profits or advantages', then in the 1620s as an adjective. The noun is now far more common than the adjective.
items.cn: 英语 beneficiary（17 世纪 10 年代）很可能经由法语 bénéficiaire 而来，先作名词“获得利润或好处的人”，17 世纪 20 年代再作形容词。如今名词用法远比形容词用法常见。

items.en: This is the key contrast with beneficial. beneficialis uses -alis to make 'pertaining to a benefit', a quality adjective. beneficiarius uses -arius to make 'the person who enjoys a benefit', a personal noun. Same base, different suffix, different word class.
items.cn: 这是它与 beneficial 的关键差别。beneficialis 用 -alis 构成“与好处有关的”性质形容词；beneficiarius 用 -arius 构成“享有好处的人”这一指人名词。同一词基，不同后缀，不同词性。

items.en: Modern English pushed the noun into law and finance: wills, life insurance, trusts, letters of credit, third-party contract rights. The old adjective use faded, and the attributive use in beneficiary country is a noun adjunct, not a revival of the adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个名词推入法律与金融：遗嘱、人寿保险、信托、信用证、合同第三方权利。旧的形容词用法衰落了；beneficiary country 里的定语用法是名词作定语，并不是旧形容词的复活。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin base but differs in suffix and direction (giver or receiver); the second group contains words for receivers that differ in legal status and setting.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词基，但后缀和方向不同（给予者还是接受者）；第二组都是“接受者”，但法律身份与场景不同。

entries.definition: Producing a good effect. It is an adjective, so it can never stand for the person who receives; -ial marks quality, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 产生良好效果的。它是形容词，绝不能代替接受者本人；-ial 标记性质，不指人。

entries.definition: Kind and generous in character. It points at the person who does good, the opposite direction from beneficiary.
entries.definitionCN: 生性仁慈慷慨的。它指向行善的人，方向与 beneficiary 相反。

entries.definition: A church office with its income. It looks like beneficiary shortened, but it comes from the 'office granted' branch of beneficium.
entries.definitionCN: 带收入的教会圣职。它看起来像 beneficiary 的缩短形式，但来自 beneficium“授予的职位”这一分支。

entries.definition: A person who gives help or money. Benefactor gives; beneficiary receives; the -fact- of benefactor is the 'do' of facere.
entries.definitionCN: 提供帮助或金钱的人。benefactor 给，beneficiary 收；benefactor 里的 -fact- 就是 facere 的“做”。

entries.definition: Anyone who receives something. It is neutral and carries no legal entitlement, whereas beneficiary implies a recognized right to the benefit.
entries.definitionCN: 任何接受某物的人。它是中性的，不含法律权利；而 beneficiary 暗示对该利益有被承认的权利。

entries.definition: A person who inherits property by law or blood relationship, whether or not a will names them.
entries.definitionCN: 依法定或血缘继承财产的人，无论遗嘱是否点名。

entries.definition: A person who receives a legacy, usually money or movable property, under a will. Narrower than beneficiary, which also covers insurance and trusts.
entries.definitionCN: 依遗嘱接受遗赠（通常是钱或动产）的人。比 beneficiary 窄，后者还涵盖保险与信托。

entries.definition: The party to whom a payment is made, especially on a cheque or bill. It names only the receiving end of a payment.
entries.definitionCN: 收款的一方，尤指支票或票据上的收款人。它只命名付款的接收端。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real documents and real contrasts with the giver's word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀、真实的文书，以及和“给予者”一词的真实对比。

normal.en: -ary marks a person attached to something; in beneficiary that person is attached to a benefit, while -ial in beneficial marks a quality instead.
normal.cn: -ary 标记附着于某物的人；在 beneficiary 里此人与“好处”相连，而 beneficial 的 -ial 标记的是性质。

normal.en: Three documents always have a beneficiary line: a will, an insurance policy, and a trust deed.
normal.cn: 三种文书总有受益人栏：遗嘱、保单、信托契约。

normal.en: Direction test: benefactor gives, beneficiary receives. If the sentence is about giving, it is the wrong word.
normal.cn: 方向测试：benefactor 给，beneficiary 收。如果句子讲的是“给”，那就用错了词。

normal.en: Same stem as beneficial, different suffix: -ary makes a person, -ial makes a quality.
normal.cn: 与 beneficial 同词干、不同后缀：-ary 造人，-ial 造性质。

normal.en: In a letter of credit the form itself names the beneficiary, so banking gives the word a concrete place.
normal.cn: 在信用证里，表格本身就要填 beneficiary，银行业务给了这个词一个具体的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a document with an arrow leaving the page and landing on a person: the person at the arrow's end is the beneficiary.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件，一支箭头离开纸面落在一个人身上：箭头末端的那个人就是 beneficiary。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs facing each other: the giver's chair is benefactor, the receiver's chair is beneficiary.
abstract.cn: 想象两把面对面的椅子：给予者的椅子是 benefactor，接受者的椅子是 beneficiary。

abstract.en: Picture a name written on a line: the line is the channel through which the benefit flows, and the name is the person at its end.
abstract.cn: 想象一条横线上写着一个名字：这条线是利益流动的通道，名字就是通道末端的人。

examples.en: She left the house to her nephew as the sole beneficiary of her will.
examples.cn: 她把房子留给侄子，作为她遗嘱的唯一受益人。

examples.en: The insurance company paid the beneficiary within thirty days.
examples.cn: 保险公司在三十天内向受益人支付了赔款。

examples.en: Rural households were the main beneficiaries of the electrification programme.
examples.cn: 农村家庭是电气化项目的主要受益者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 本（ben）来的好处（benefit）舍（she）给谁，谁就是 beneficiary 受益人

root: 拉丁 bene“好”+ facere“做” → beneficium“恩惠” → beneficiarius“受恩惠者、享有特权者”；-ary 表“与……有关的人”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one position: the person at the receiving end of a benefit. What changes is the document that assigns it — a will, a policy, a trust, a contract, a payment order — or, in the loosest sense, no document at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个位置：处在利益接受端的那个人。变化的是分配利益的那份文书——遗嘱、保单、信托、合同、付款指令——或者在最宽松的义项里，根本没有文书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a named person at the receiving end of a benefit written into a document.
core.cn: 核心意象：写在文书里的利益，末端是一个具名的接受者。

branches.en: PRIVATE AND CHARITABLE RECEIVERS: a will names an heir; a charity names the person it helps.
branches.cn: 私人与慈善接受者：遗嘱点名继承人；慈善机构点名它帮助的人。

branches.en: POLICY AND TRUST: the nomination or the trust deed assigns the benefit to a named party.
branches.cn: 保单与信托：指定或信托契据把利益分配给具名的一方。

branches.en: PAYMENT AND CONTRACT: banking and contract law make the beneficiary a technical party with a right to enforce.
branches.cn: 付款与合同：银行和合同法使 beneficiary 成为有主张权的技术性当事方。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND ATTRIBUTIVE: whole countries and households become the receiving side of a programme.
branches.cn: 集体与定语用法：整个国家与家庭成为项目的接受方。

branches.en: LOOSE EXTENSION: anyone who profits from an event, with no document at all.
branches.cn: 宽松延伸：任何从事件中获利的人，完全不需要文书。

intro.en: Beneficiary is bene- + -fic- + -ary, and each piece is still readable: 'well' + 'doing' + 'person connected with'. The -ary ending is the decisive one, because it turns a benefit into a person.
intro.cn: beneficiary 是 bene- + -fic- + -ary，每一块至今仍可读：“好”+“做”+“与之相连的人”。决定性的是 -ary，因为它把“好处”变成了“人”。

latinIntro.en: Latin bene and facere also produced beneficium, beneficus and beneficiarius. English keeps the -ary branch for people (beneficiary) and the -ial branch for qualities (beneficial), a split inherited from Latin suffix choice.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 bene 和 facere 还产生了 beneficium、beneficus、beneficiarius。英语把 -ary 那一支留给指人（beneficiary），把 -ial 那一支留给性质（beneficial），这一分裂承自拉丁语的后缀选择。

items.meaning: an advantage; to help or gain
items.example: The scholarship brought a real benefit to her family.
items.exampleCN: 这笔奖学金给她家带来了实实在在的好处。

items.example: The change was beneficial to the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 这一变化对整个团队都有益。

items.meaning: a person who receives a benefit
items.example: The beneficiary must show proof of identity.
items.exampleCN: 受益人必须出示身份证明。

items.meaning: one who gives help or money
items.example: A benefactor funded the new laboratory.
items.exampleCN: 一位捐助者出资修建了新实验室。

items.example: The clinic depends on the beneficence of donors.
items.exampleCN: 这家诊所依靠捐助者的善心维持。

items.example: A beneficent stranger paid for the medicine.
items.exampleCN: 一位好心的陌生人付了药费。

items.meaning: a church office with its income
items.example: The bishop granted him a benefice.
items.exampleCN: 主教授予他一处圣职俸禄。

items.meaning: the formal act of naming a beneficiary
items.meaningCN: 受益人指定（正式指定受益人的行为）
items.example: A beneficiary designation must be signed and dated.
items.exampleCN: 受益人指定必须签名并注明日期。

items.example: The maleficent spell brought illness to the village.
items.exampleCN: 恶毒的咒语给村庄带来了疾病。

items.example: They manufacture medical devices in this plant.
items.exampleCN: 他们在这座工厂生产医疗器械。

latinEntries.meaning: a favor, service, kindness; a granted office
latinEntries.meaningCN: 恩惠；服务；善意；授予的职位

definition_zh: n. 弓；蝴蝶结；琴弓；v. 用弓拉奏；鞠躬（读 /baʊ/）
definition_en: a weapon made of a curved piece of wood and a string; also a knot with two loops, or the rod used to play a violin
core_image: 一张弯木弓被弦拉成满月
scene: 弓箭手把弓拉成满月，屏住呼吸。 The archer drew the bow and held her breath.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bow 指射箭用的弓；句意是弓箭手把弓拉满，屏住呼吸。

pos.zh: 弓；蝴蝶结；琴弓
用弓拉奏；鞠躬（读 /baʊ/）

senses.title: A weapon for shooting arrows
senses.definition: a curved piece of wood with a tight string, used to shoot arrows
senses.definitionCN: 弯曲木料绷紧弓弦、用来射箭的武器
senses.example: He practised with a wooden bow every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上用木弓练习。
senses.why: The archery noun is /bəʊ/; the bending verb in sense 04 is /baʊ/.
senses.whyCN: 射箭用的名词读 /bəʊ/；第 4 个义项里表示弯腰的动词读 /baʊ/。

senses.title: A knot with two loops
senses.definition: a ribbon or string tied into two loops, used on shoes or gifts
senses.definitionCN: 系成两个环的丝带或绳结，用于鞋或礼物
senses.example: The parcel was tied with a red bow.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹用红丝带系了个蝴蝶结。
senses.why: The curve of the bent wood carries over to the bent ribbon.
senses.whyCN: 弯木的弧线延用到了弯曲的丝带上。

senses.title: A rod for playing strings
senses.definition: a long thin rod with stretched hair, drawn across the strings of a violin
senses.definitionCN: 绷着马尾毛、在小提琴弦上拉动的长细杆
senses.example: Rosin the bow before the first note.
senses.exampleCN: 拉第一个音之前给琴弓上松香。
senses.why: The same curve and tension appear in a small wooden rod.
senses.whyCN: 同样的小木杆上也有相同的弧线与张力。

senses.title: To bend the head in greeting
senses.definition: to lower the head or upper body as a sign of respect, pronounced /baʊ/
senses.definitionCN: 以低头或弯腰表示敬意，读作 /baʊ/
senses.example: The actors bowed to the audience.
senses.exampleCN: 演员们向观众鞠躬。
senses.why: This verb shares the bending root but keeps a different vowel.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词与「弯曲」同根，却保留了不同的元音。

intro.en: Bow comes from an Old English word for a bent thing, from a root meaning to bend.
intro.cn: bow 源自表示弯曲之物的古英语词，词根意为弯曲。

items.en: Boga means a bow, from a root meaning to bend.
items.cn: boga 意为弓，词根意为弯曲。

items.en: Bugan means to bend the body.
items.cn: bugan 意为弯身。

items.en: Bowe covers both the weapon and the bending.
items.cn: bowe 兼指武器与弯腰。

items.en: The longbow changes warfare in England.
items.cn: 长弓改变了英格兰的战争形态。

items.en: The bow becomes standard for string instruments.
items.cn: 琴弓成为弦乐器的标准用具。

items.en: The bow tie fixes the looped knot in fashion.
items.cn: 领结让双环结成为服饰元素。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on the two pronunciations; the near-meaning group comes from archery and from shape.
note.cn: 形近组围绕两种读音；近义组则来自射箭与形状两方面。

definition_zh: n. 军备，武器装备（总称）；（舰船或飞机的）武器系统；武装起来的过程
definition_en: The weapons and military resources of a country or force; the guns and missile systems fitted to a ship or aircraft; the process of arming for war.
core_image: 把武器一件件装到船上、机上、国库里
scene: 条约限制重型军备的部署。 The treaty limits the deployment of heavy armament.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：armament 指一国或一支力量的武器与军力总称。

pos.zh: 军备；武器系统；武装

senses.title: A country's military resources
senses.definition: the whole stock of weapons, vehicles and equipment a state or force maintains
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或一支武装力量所维持的全部武器、载具与装备
senses.example: The report compares the armament of the two alliances.
senses.exampleCN: 报告比较了两大同盟的军备。
senses.why: The suffix -ment names means or result, so armament is what arming produces: the equipment itself.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 表手段或结果，所以 armament 就是「武装」所产出的东西：装备本身。

senses.title: The guns fitted to a vessel
senses.definition: the specific guns, cannon or missile systems mounted on a ship, aircraft or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 安装在舰船、飞机或车辆上的具体火炮、舰炮或导弹系统
senses.example: The cruiser's main armament was removed after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘巡洋舰的主炮系统在战后被拆除。
senses.why: Here the word narrows from a nation to one hull: the same equipping idea applied to a single platform.
senses.whyCN: 这里词义从一国收窄到一条船：同样的「装备」概念用在单个平台上。

senses.title: The act of arming
senses.definition: the process of building up military strength, the sense behind armament race
senses.definitionCN: 扩充军力的过程，即 armament race 背后的含义
senses.example: Rapid armament followed the breakdown of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判破裂之后迅速展开了军备扩充。
senses.why: Because -ment can name an action as well as its result, the word also covers the building up, not only the stock.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -ment 既可表结果也可表动作，这个词也涵盖「扩充」本身，而不只是存量。

intro.en: Armament is Latin armamentum, equipment, from armare, to arm, plus the means suffix -mentum. English first used it for the guns of a warship.
intro.cn: armament 就是拉丁语 armamentum「装备」，由 armare「武装」加表手段的后缀 -mentum 构成。英语最初用它指战舰的火炮。

items.en: Latin arma meant weapons and gear, the base of arm, army, armour and armada.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arma 意为武器与装备，是 arm、army、armour 与 armada 的共同基础。

items.en: Armare meant to equip for fighting, whether a soldier, a ship or a fortress.
items.cn: armare 意为「为作战而装备」，对象可以是士兵、船只或堡垒。

items.en: Adding -mentum, the suffix for a means or instrument, gave armamentum, the equipment itself.
items.cn: 加上表手段或工具的后缀 -mentum 得到 armamentum，即装备本身。

items.en: English recorded armament in the 1690s for the guns carried by a warship.
items.cn: 英语在 1690 年代记录 armament，指战舰所携火炮。

items.en: Through the eighteenth century the word widened from one ship's guns to a whole state's military stock.
items.cn: 整个 18 世纪，词义从一条船的火炮扩展到一国全部的军事存量。

items.en: Twentieth-century treaties made armament and disarmament standard terms of international law.
items.cn: 20 世纪的条约使 armament 与 disarmament 成为国际法的标准用语。

note.en: The look-alike group contrasts armistice, a stop to fighting, with armament, the means of it; the near-meaning group lists other words for weapons.
note.cn: 形近组把 armistice「停战」与 armament「作战手段」对照；近义组列出其他表示武器的词。

entries.definition: An agreed stop to fighting.
entries.definitionCN: 约定停止战斗。

entries.definition: Covering that stops weapons.
entries.definitionCN: 挡住武器的护甲。

entries.definition: The rotating part of a motor.
entries.definitionCN: 电动机的转动部件。

entries.definition: A large fleet of warships.
entries.definitionCN: 大批战舰组成的舰队。

entries.definition: Weapons considered together.
entries.definitionCN: 武器的总称。

entries.definition: Ammunition and military stores.
entries.definitionCN: 弹药与军需物资。

entries.definition: Mounted guns and their supplies.
entries.definitionCN: 火炮及其补给。

entries.definition: A store of weapons, or the place.
entries.definitionCN: 武器库，或其存放处。

normalIntro.en: Armament is arm plus -ment: what arming produces, the equipment a force actually holds.
normalIntro.cn: armament 就是 arm 加 -ment：「武装」产出的东西，即一支力量实际持有的装备。

normal.en: Armament arms you; armistice stops the fighting.
normal.cn: armament 是武装，armistice 是停战。

normal.en: Disarmament is the reverse, with dis- added.
normal.cn: disarmament 是反向，加了 dis-。

normal.en: Main armament is the fixed naval term.
normal.cn: main armament 是海军固定术语。

normal.en: It can be countable when meaning systems.
normal.cn: 指武器系统时可数。

normal.en: Armament race and arms race mean the same thing.
normal.cn: armament race 与 arms race 同义。

abstract.en: Picture guns being bolted onto a deck.
abstract.cn: 想象火炮被螺栓固定到甲板上。

abstract.en: Imagine a warehouse counted line by line.
abstract.cn: 想象一间被逐行清点的库房。

abstract.en: Think of two states stacking weight on a scale.
abstract.cn: 想象两国在天平两端不断加砝码。

examples.en: The ship carried a modest armament for its size.
examples.cn: 以吨位而言，这艘船的武器配置不算多。

examples.en: Both sides pledged to cut their armaments.
examples.cn: 双方承诺削减各自军备。

examples.en: The treaty froze further armament in the region.
examples.cn: 条约冻结了该地区的进一步军备扩充。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arm「武器」+ -ment「手段、结果」——武装出来的装备，就是军备 armament。

root: 拉丁语 arma「武器」生出 armare「武装」，加表手段的后缀 -mentum 成 armamentum「装备」；英语 1690 年代先指舰炮，后扩展为一国军备。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses follow one equipping: the stock a nation holds, the guns on one hull, and the act of building the stock up.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项沿着同一次「装备」展开：一国持有的存量、一条船上的火炮，以及把存量堆起来的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: weapons being fitted one by one onto ships, planes and into stores
core.cn: 核心意象：把武器一件件装到船上、机上、国库里

branches.en: Two alliances counted weapon by weapon.
branches.cn: 逐件清点武器的两大同盟。

branches.en: A cruiser stripped of its main guns.
branches.cn: 主炮被拆掉的巡洋舰。

branches.en: Missiles fitted under a wing.
branches.cn: 挂在机翼下的导弹。

branches.en: Rapid build-up after talks collapse.
branches.cn: 谈判破裂后的迅速扩充。

branches.en: Both name what arming produces.
branches.cn: 两者都指「武装」所产出的东西。

intro.en: Armament is arm plus -ment, and with dis- it flips to disarm and disarmament; the root also builds armour and army.
intro.cn: armament 是 arm 加 -ment，加上 dis- 就翻转为 disarm 与 disarmament；同一词根还构成 armour 与 army。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arma, armare and armamentum; -mentum is the Latin suffix for a means or instrument.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arma、armare 与 armamentum；-mentum 是拉丁语表手段或工具的后缀。

definition_zh: 两足动物；两足行走的动物；两足的（形容词用法）
definition_en: an animal that walks on two feet; two-footed
core_image: 恐龙与人类同框：都是踩着两只脚走路
scene: 展厅里，恐龙骨架和人骨架并排站立。 Humans are bipeds, unlike their four-footed cousins.
sceneCN: 这里 biped 是「两足动物」（第 1 个义项：以两脚行走的动物）；句意是与其四足的远亲不同，人类是两足动物。

pos.zh: 两足动物
两足的

derivatives.zh: biped 加 -al，义为「两足的；用两足行走的」
bipedal 加 -ism，义为「两足行走习性」
同族反义词，义为「四足动物」
同根词，义为「踏板」，来自 pes「足」

senses.title: An animal walking on two feet
senses.definition: a creature that habitually moves about on two legs
senses.definitionCN: 惯于用两条腿移动的动物
senses.example: Humans are bipeds, unlike their four-footed cousins.
senses.exampleCN: 与其四足的远亲不同，人类是两足动物。
senses.why: Latin bi- means two and pes means foot: two-footed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 bi- 意为「二」，pes 意为「足」，合即「双足」。

senses.title: A bird as a two-footed creature
senses.definition: any bird, whose only limbs for walking are its two feet
senses.definitionCN: 泛指以两足为行走器官的鸟类
senses.example: Every sparrow is a feathered biped.
senses.exampleCN: 每只麻雀都是有羽毛的两足动物。
senses.why: Zoology counts feet: birds have exactly two.
senses.whyCN: 动物学按足计数：鸟类恰好两只。

senses.title: Dinosaurs that ran on hind legs
senses.titleCN: （兽脚类恐龙）两足行走的恐龙
senses.definition: a dinosaur of groups that moved on their hind limbs
senses.definitionCN: 以后肢行走的恐龙类群
senses.example: Tyrannosaurs were powerful bipeds.
senses.exampleCN: 暴龙是有力的两足动物。
senses.why: Paleontology adopted the foot-count for dinosaurs.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学以足数命名恐龙姿态。

senses.title: Two-footed as adjective
senses.definition: two-footed, used attributively
senses.definitionCN: 作定语用的「两足的」
senses.example: The biped robot took its first steps.
senses.exampleCN: 这台两足机器人迈出了第一步。
senses.why: The noun doubles as an adjective in engineering.
senses.whyCN: 在工程语境中该名词兼作形容词。

senses.title: A human being (formal or playful)
senses.definition: a human, viewed humorously or formally as a two-footed animal
senses.definitionCN: 以两足动物之名正式或戏谑地指人
senses.example: The picnic fed twenty hungry bipeds.
senses.exampleCN: 野餐喂饱了二十个饥肠辘辘的两足动物。
senses.why: Man is the everyday biped, so the word can point at us.
senses.whyCN: 人是最寻常的两足动物，故该词可指向我们。

senses.title: Robots on two legs
senses.definition: a walking robot with two leg mechanisms
senses.definitionCN: 装有两足行走机构的机器人
senses.example: Engineers tuned the biped's balance.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师调试双足机器人的平衡。
senses.why: Robotics borrows zoology's foot-count.
senses.whyCN: 机器人学借用动物学的足数分类。

senses.title: Habitual versus occasional bipedalism
senses.definition: an animal defined by regular two-footed movement, as opposed to occasional stance
senses.definitionCN: 以经常性两足移动定义的动物，区别于偶尔站立
senses.example: Chimps stand up often but are not true bipeds.
senses.exampleCN: 黑猩猩常站起来，但并非真正的两足动物。
senses.why: Habit, not moment, fixes the class.
senses.whyCN: 决定类别的在于习性而非瞬间。

senses.title: In evolutionary argument
senses.definition: bipedalism as a marker in debates on human origins
senses.definitionCN: 两足行走作为人类起源争论中的标志特征
senses.example: Fossil feet settled when our line became bipeds.
senses.exampleCN: 足部化石确定了我们的谱系何时成为两足动物。
senses.why: Feet in fossils testify to the two-footed turn.
senses.whyCN: 化石中的足部为「双足转向」作证。

definition_zh: 在……之前；先于；在……以前（较正式）
definition_en: before a particular time, event or action, used in formal and technical writing
core_image: 手术推车停在门口，墙上的钟还差一格才到开始时刻
scene: 手术室外的推车停在门口，护士核对腕带与同意书。 All patients must fast prior to the operation.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（在时间上先于某事件）；句意为所有病人都必须在手术之前禁食。

pos.zh: 介词性短语：在……之前；先于
相关形容词：先前的；优先的

由该名词加动词词尾构成，义为「按优先级排列；优先处理」
由该动词加表示动作结果的名词词尾构成，义为「优先排序」

senses.title: Before a point in time
senses.definition: earlier than a stated time, date or event
senses.definitionCN: 早于某个指明的时间、日期或事件
senses.example: All applications must be filed prior to the first of March.
senses.exampleCN: 所有申请都必须在三月一日之前提交。
senses.why: Prior is the comparative of a word for before, so the phrase places one thing ahead of another on the timeline.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是比较级形式，词干意为「在前」，因此该短语把一件事放到时间线上另一件事的前面。

senses.title: Formal substitute for before
senses.definition: used in place of the plainer preposition in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中替代更朴素的介词
senses.example: Prior to the merger, the two firms were direct rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 合并之前，这两家公司是直接的竞争对手。
senses.why: Documents often prefer a heavier phrase to a plain one, and this is the standard heavier choice.
senses.whyCN: 文书常用更厚重的短语代替朴素说法，这就是标准的厚重选择。

senses.title: Earlier in a procedure
senses.definition: marking the step that must be completed before the next one
senses.definitionCN: 标示必须在下一步之前完成的那一步
senses.example: The sample is weighed prior to drying.
senses.exampleCN: 样品在干燥之前先称重。
senses.why: A procedure is a sequence, and the phrase fixes which step comes first.
senses.whyCN: 流程是一个序列，这个短语固定了哪一步在前。

senses.title: Before doing something
senses.definition: followed by a gerund to name an action that must happen first
senses.definitionCN: 后接动名词，指出必须先发生的动作
senses.example: Prior to signing, read every clause aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 签署之前，把每一条款朗读一遍。
senses.why: The preposition takes a noun, so a verb must be turned into a gerund before it can follow.
senses.whyCN: 这个介词要接名词，所以动词必须先变成动名词才能跟在后面。

senses.title: Before a date in contracts
senses.definition: used in contracts to fix a deadline before a stated date
senses.definitionCN: 在合同中确定某一日期之前的期限
senses.example: Rent is payable prior to the fifth day of each month.
senses.exampleCN: 租金须在每月第五日之前支付。
senses.why: Legal drafting needs a phrase that cannot be confused with after, and this one is unambiguous.
senses.whyCN: 法律起草需要一个不会与「之后」混淆的短语，这个短语毫不含糊。

senses.title: Before an observation in research
senses.definition: marking preparation that must precede measurement or testing
senses.definitionCN: 标示必须先于测量或测试完成的准备
senses.example: The instrument is calibrated prior to each run.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器在每次运行之前都要校准。
senses.why: Experimental method insists on order, and the phrase records that order in the protocol.
senses.whyCN: 实验方法强调次序，这个短语把该次序写进规程。

senses.title: Earlier in a sequence of events
senses.definition: used in narrative to place one event ahead of another
senses.definitionCN: 在叙述中把一件事放在另一件事之前
senses.example: The alarm sounded prior to the collapse, giving crews time to leave.
senses.exampleCN: 坍塌之前警报响了，为工人争取到撤离时间。
senses.why: Narrative uses the phrase to mark a warning that came early enough to matter.
senses.whyCN: 叙述用这个短语标记一个来得够早、因而起了作用的预警。

senses.title: Before arriving or departing
senses.definition: used of formal requirements that apply before a journey or an arrival
senses.definitionCN: 用于出发或到达之前必须满足的正式要求
senses.example: Passengers should check in prior to boarding.
senses.exampleCN: 旅客应在登机之前办理手续。
senses.why: Travel rules are written formally, and the phrase marks the deadline before the vehicle leaves.
senses.whyCN: 出行规定写得正式，这个短语标出交通工具离开之前的截止点。

intro.en: Prior comes from Latin prior, former or earlier, the comparative of a stem seen in prae, before. English first used it as a noun for a monastic superior and later as an adjective; the phrase prior to is a modern formal replacement for before.
intro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语中意为「先前的、更早的」比较级形式，其词干见于表示「在前」的介词。英语先把它用作修院职名，后用作形容词；这个短语是近代对更朴素介词的正式替代。

items.en: Prae meant before or in front, and it is the stem behind the comparative prior.
items.cn: 这个词意为「在前、在……之前」，是比较级形式的词干来源。

items.en: Prior was the comparative of that stem, meaning former or earlier, and also a person set above others.
items.cn: 这个词是上述词干的比较级，意为先前的、更早的，也指位居他人之上者。

items.en: The Church used the noun for the head of a house, and French passed that noun to English.
items.cn: 教会用这个名词指修院之首，法语又把该名词传入英语。

items.en: From the sixteenth century English also used it plainly as earlier, beside the noun.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，英语也把它单纯用作「更早的」，与名词义并存。

items.en: The prepositional phrase spread in formal and legal writing in the nineteenth century; its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个介词短语在十九世纪的正式与法律文书中扩散；确切的书面首见年代不确定。

items.en: Today it is standard in documents, medicine and engineering, where the plainer word would sound too casual.
items.cn: 今天它常见于文书、医学与工程文本，在这些场合更朴素的近义介词显得太随意。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin comparative or its word family; the second group lists other ways of saying before.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一个拉丁比较级或其词族；第二组是表示「在……之前」的其他说法。

entries.definition: The adjective inside the phrase, meaning earlier or more important.
entries.definitionCN: 短语内部的形容词，义为更早的或更重要的。

entries.definition: The noun built on the adjective, meaning first place or a matter ranked first.
entries.definitionCN: 由该形容词构成的名词，义为优先地位或首要事项。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to rank things in order of importance.
entries.definitionCN: 义为按重要程度排序的动词。

entries.definition: A religious house ruled by a prior, built on the older noun sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由更早的名词义构成，指由修院院长管理的小修道院。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning before, from the same Latin stem.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「在前」的前缀，出自同一拉丁词干。

entries.definition: The plain everyday preposition that the phrase replaces in formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 朴素的日常介词，正式文字中用该短语替代它。

entries.definition: A comparative phrase that compares two times directly.
entries.definitionCN: 比较级短语，直接比较两个时间。

entries.definition: A phrase for position in front, used of time as well as space.
entries.definitionCN: 表示位于前方的短语，时间和空间都可用。

entries.definition: An adjective for the thing that comes just before another.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指紧挨在另一事物之前的那一个。

entries.definition: A phrase stressing preparation made before an event.
entries.definitionCN: 强调在事件之前完成准备的短语。

normalIntro.en: Prior is the comparative of before: one thing stands ahead of another, and the phrase fixes that order.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「在前」的比较级：一件事站在另一件之前，这个短语把这次序固定下来。

normal.en: A gurney at the theatre door while the clock is still one mark short of the start.
normal.cn: 手术推车停在门口，墙上的钟还差一格才到开始时刻。

normal.en: Prior means earlier, so the phrase simply says earlier than a point.
normal.cn: 这个词意为更早的，所以短语就是「早于某一点」。

normal.en: In documents it replaces the plain word before and sounds more formal.
normal.cn: 在文书里它替代朴素的近义介词，听起来更正式。

normal.en: A verb after it must wear the ing ending, because a preposition takes a noun.
normal.cn: 它后面的动词必须加表示进行的词尾，因为介词要接名词。

normal.en: In contracts it usually points at a date, not at a person.
normal.cn: 在合同里它通常指向某个日期，而不是某个人。

abstract.en: To say prior to is to admit that order is part of meaning.
abstract.cn: 说「在……之前」，就是承认次序本身也是意义的一部分。

abstract.en: Formal language often pays for precision with extra weight.
abstract.cn: 正式语言常以更厚重的形式来换取精确。

abstract.en: Everything that must happen first is already a condition.
abstract.cn: 凡必须先发生的事，本身就已经是一个条件。

examples.en: All applications must be filed prior to the first of March.
examples.cn: 所有申请都必须在三月一日之前提交。

examples.en: The instrument is calibrated prior to each run.
examples.cn: 仪器在每次运行之前都要校准。

examples.en: Prior to signing, read every clause aloud.
examples.cn: 签署之前，把每一条款朗读一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普莱尔 图」——「普莱尔」是在前的，「图」朝向那一点：在……之前

root: 拉丁语比较级形式，义为「更早的、在先的」，词干见于表示「在前」的介词；英语先用作修院职名，后作形容词，短语为近代正式替代说法，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one core idea, earlier than a point, and vary the setting: plain time, formal prose, procedures, gerunds, contracts, experiments, narrative and travel.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个核心意思，即早于某一点，只是场景不同：单纯时间、正式文字、流程、动名词、合同、实验、叙述与出行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gurney waiting at the theatre door while the clock is still one mark short of the start.
core.cn: 核心意象：手术推车停在门口，墙上的钟还差一格才到开始时刻。

branches.en: TIME BEFORE: the phrase marks an earlier point and replaces the plainer word in formal prose.
branches.cn: 时间在先：标示更早的时点，并在正式文字中替代更朴素的说法。

branches.en: STEP BEFORE: in procedures and experiments one act must come first.
branches.cn: 步骤在先：流程与实验中，某一动作必须先做。

branches.en: ACTION BEFORE: a gerund names what must be done earlier.
branches.cn: 动作在先：动名词指出必须先做的事。

branches.en: DATE BEFORE: contracts fix a deadline by means of the phrase.
branches.cn: 日期在先：合同借这个短语设定截止期限。

branches.en: EVENT BEFORE: in a narrative the phrase places one event ahead of another.
branches.cn: 事件在先：叙述中把一件事放在另一件事之前。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a Latin comparative adjective plus a native preposition. The items below show the family and the constructions it enters.
intro.cn: 这个短语由拉丁比较级形容词加本土介词构成。下列条目展示它的词族与它进入的结构。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries are prior and the preposition prae; the related superlative primus explains the wider family but is not the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 列出的拉丁词条是比较级形式与介词；相关的最高级形式解释了更大的词族，但并非直接来源。

items.example: It supplies the meaning of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它提供这个短语的意义。

items.example: It is the stem behind the comparative.
items.exampleCN: 它是比较级背后的词干。

items.example: It belongs to the same family but is not the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 它属于同一词族，但不是直接来源。

items.meaning: first place, a matter ranked first
items.example: It turns the adjective into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成抽象名词。

items.meaning: to rank in order of importance
items.example: It turns the noun into an action.
The action noun is built on the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个动作名词由动词构成。

items.meaning: a house ruled by a prior
items.example: It keeps the older noun sense of a superior.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了「上位者」这一较早的名词义。

items.example: The phrase takes a noun or a noun phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语接名词或名词短语。

items.example: A verb must become a gerund after the preposition.
items.exampleCN: 介词后的动词必须变成动名词。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加名词词尾构成，义为「优先；首要事项」
由该名词加动词词尾构成，义为「按优先级排列」
由该动词加名词词尾构成，义为「优先排序」
由同族名词加表示场所的词尾构成，义为「小修道院」

definition_zh: 龙卷风；陆龙卷；（旧义）雷暴；旋风般的一阵
definition_en: a violently rotating column of air extending from a thundercloud to the ground
core_image: 漏斗状的黑云从雷暴底部垂到地面，所过之处尘土、木板与树枝被卷上天
scene: 警报器在镇上响起，人们抱着孩子跑向地下室，广播员喊道 A tornado touched down in the wheat field west of town.
sceneCN: 这里 tornado 指「从雷暴云伸到地面的旋转空气柱」（第 1 个义项：气象学意义上的陆龙卷）；句意为一个龙卷风在镇子西边的小麦田里触地。

pos.zh: 龙卷风；陆龙卷；旋风般的一阵

collocations.zh: 龙卷风警报（已发现龙卷风）
龙卷风警戒（条件可能形成）

derivatives.zh: 龙卷风的；具有龙卷风特征的

senses.title: Rotating column touching the ground
senses.titleCN: 陆龙卷：触地的旋转空气柱
senses.definition: a violently rotating column of air in contact with both a thundercloud and the ground
senses.definitionCN: 同时接触雷暴云与地面的猛烈旋转空气柱
senses.example: The tornado flattened two barns in less than a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 龙卷风不到一分钟就推平了两座谷仓。
senses.why: The meteorological definition turns on ground contact: a funnel that never touches down is not counted as one.
senses.whyCN: 气象学定义的关键在是否触地：始终没触地的漏斗云不算龙卷风。

senses.title: Any violent whirlwind
senses.definition: in everyday speech, any destructive whirling wind, whatever its origin
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语中泛指任何破坏性的旋转风，不论其成因
senses.example: A tornado of dust crossed the road and blinded the drivers.
senses.exampleCN: 一团尘土旋风横过公路，让司机们看不见路。
senses.why: Ordinary speakers name the visible violence rather than the classification, so the word widens beyond the technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 普通人按可见的暴力命名，而不按分类，因此这个词超出技术义。

senses.title: Old sense: a thunderstorm
senses.definition: in sixteenth- and seventeenth-century English, a violent thunderstorm rather than a funnel
senses.definitionCN: 在 16 与 17 世纪英语中，指猛烈的雷暴而非漏斗云
senses.example: In the old chronicle a tornado broke the masts of three ships.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部旧编年史里，一场雷暴折断了三艘船的桅杆。
senses.why: The word came from Spanish for a thunderstorm; the modern funnel sense narrowed from that wider weather event much later.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自西班牙语中「雷暴」的说法；现代漏斗义是后来从这一更宽的天气事件收窄出来的。

senses.title: West African squall line
senses.titleCN: 西非常见用法：飑线雷暴
senses.definition: in West African English, a line of violent thunderstorms with sudden cool wind
senses.definitionCN: 西非英语中指伴随骤起凉风的强雷暴线
senses.example: The harmattan tornado rolled in from the savannah at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时，来自稀树草原的雷暴飑线滚滚而来。
senses.why: Regional usage kept the older broad sense, so the same word names a thunder line on another continent.
senses.whyCN: 地域用法保留了较早的宽泛义，因此同一个词在另一块大陆指雷暴线。

senses.title: The disaster event
senses.titleCN: 作为灾害事件的龙卷风
senses.definition: the storm viewed as an event that destroys buildings and takes lives
senses.definitionCN: 从摧毁建筑、夺走生命的灾害事件角度看的龙卷风
senses.example: The tornado killed eleven people on the edge of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这场龙卷风在城市边缘夺走了十一条生命。
senses.why: Reports and insurance claims treat the vortex as a single catastrophic event, and the word follows that usage.
senses.whyCN: 报道与保险理赔把涡旋当作单一灾难点，这个词也随之这样用。

senses.title: Figurative burst
senses.definition: a sudden overwhelming burst of applause, criticism or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 掌声、批评或情绪突然而压倒性的一阵爆发
senses.example: A tornado of applause met the singer at the end of the song.
senses.exampleCN: 歌曲结束时，一阵暴风般的掌声迎向歌手。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the shape: something arrives spinning, fast, and sweeps everything up.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了形状：某物旋转着快速到来，把一切卷起。

senses.title: Tornado season
senses.definition: the spring period in which tornadoes are most frequent in a region
senses.definitionCN: 某地区龙卷风最频繁的春季时段
senses.example: The plains grow quiet again after tornado season ends.
senses.exampleCN: 龙卷风季结束后，平原又安静下来。
senses.why: The season is named for its dominant hazard, a common pattern in weather vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 季节以主导灾害命名，这是天气词汇常见的模式。

senses.title: The aircraft name
senses.definition: a twin-engine combat aircraft produced in Europe, known by the proper name Tornado
senses.definitionCN: 欧洲联合研制的双发战斗机，以专名 Tornado（狂风）称呼
senses.example: The Tornado flew low over the valley on a training sortie.
senses.exampleCN: 狂风战斗机在一次训练飞行中低空掠过山谷。
senses.why: Weapon names borrow the force of natural phenomena, so the storm word becomes a proper name for a machine.
senses.whyCN: 武器命名借用自然现象的威力，因此风暴词成了机器的专名。

intro.en: Tornado is a blend of two Spanish weather words: tronada 'thunderstorm', from tronar 'to thunder', and tornado 'turned, rotating', from tornar 'to turn'. English borrowed it as a word for a thunderstorm and only later narrowed it to the funnel.
intro.cn: tornado 由两个西班牙语天气词混合而成：tronada「雷暴」（来自 tronar「打雷」）与 tornado「旋转的」（来自 tornar「转」）。英语借入时指雷暴，后来才收窄为漏斗云。

items.en: Latin tonare 'to thunder', with the noun tonitrus 'thunder', supplied the first half of the Spanish word.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tonare「打雷」及其名词 tonitrus「雷」提供了西班牙语词的前半部分。

items.en: Spanish tronada meant 'thunderstorm', built on tronar 'to thunder'; it named the whole storm, not a funnel.
items.cn: 西班牙语 tronada 意为「雷暴」，由 tronar「打雷」构成；它指整场风暴，而非漏斗。

items.en: Separately, tornar 'to turn' (from Latin tornare) produced tornado 'turned, rotating'; English speakers blended the two Spanish forms.
items.cn: 另一方面，tornar「转」（来自拉丁 tornare）构成 tornado「旋转的」；英语使用者把两个西班牙语形式混合起来。

items.en: Early English records use tornado for a violent thunderstorm at sea, especially in accounts of the Caribbean and the Atlantic.
items.cn: 早期英语记载用 tornado 指海上猛烈的雷暴，尤见于加勒比与大西洋的记述。

items.en: The narrow funnel sense established itself in the nineteenth century, once observers began requiring contact with the ground.
items.cn: 狭窄的漏斗义在 19 世纪确立，因为观测者开始要求它必须触地。

note.en: The first group looks similar in spelling but comes from other roots; the second group holds the rotating-wind family and its synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组拼写相近但词根不同；第二组是旋转风家族及其同义词。

entries.definition: From Latin torpedo 'numbness, the numb fish'; it names a underwater weapon, with no turning or thunder in its root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 torpedo「麻木、电鱼」；指水下武器，词根里没有转或雷。

entries.definition: From Spanish torear 'to fight bulls', from toro 'bull'; the ending -dor marks an agent, not a storm.
entries.definitionCN: 来自西班牙语 torear「斗牛」，源于 toro「公牛」；词尾 -dor 表施事者，不是风暴。

entries.definition: The past participle of tear 'to rip'; it looks close but belongs to a completely different verb.
entries.definitionCN: tear「撕」的过去分词；形近但属于完全不同的动词。

entries.definition: From Latin torrens 'rushing, burning', from torrere 'to scorch'; it names a fast stream, not a wind.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 torrens「奔流、灼烧」，源于 torrere「烤焦」；指急流，不是风。

entries.definition: A general term for a rapidly rotating mass of air, often smaller and less organised than a tornado.
entries.definitionCN: 快速旋转气团的通称，通常比龙卷风更小、更有组织性更弱。

entries.definition: A large low-pressure system with rotating winds, hundreds of times wider than a tornado.
entries.definitionCN: 带旋转风的大型低压系统，宽度可达龙卷风的数百倍。

entries.definition: A tropical storm of the Atlantic with sustained winds above 119 km/h; a different scale of phenomenon.
entries.definitionCN: 大西洋持续风速超过每小时 119 公里的热带风暴；现象尺度不同。

entries.definition: An informal American word for a tornado, used mostly in news headlines and speech.
entries.definitionCN: 美式口语中对龙卷风的说法，多用于新闻标题与口语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Spanish blend, real meteorological terms and the real compound family, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：西班牙语混合来源、真实气象术语与真实复合词族，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: tronada 'thunderstorm' plus tornado 'turned': a storm that turns.
normal.cn: tronada「雷暴」加 tornado「旋转的」：一场会转的风暴。

normal.en: The same thunder root sits in detonate and tonitrus.
normal.cn: 同一个「雷」词根在 detonate 与 tonitrus 里。

normal.en: Warning means it has been seen; watch means it might form.
normal.cn: warning 表示已经发现；watch 表示可能形成。

normal.en: Tornado alley is the plains strip where they are most frequent.
normal.cn: tornado alley 是龙卷风最频繁的平原狭长地带。

normal.en: The plural is usually tornadoes, sometimes tornados.
normal.cn: 复数通常写 tornadoes，有时写 tornados。

abstract.en: Picture a black funnel stitching the cloud to the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一个黑色漏斗把云和地面缝在一起。

abstract.en: Picture straw driven into a wooden post by the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一根稻草被风钉进木柱。

abstract.en: Picture applause arriving like weather through a theatre.
abstract.cn: 想象掌声像天气一样扫过剧场。

examples.en: A tornado watch was issued for the whole county by noon.
examples.cn: 到中午时，整个县都发布了龙卷风警戒。

examples.en: The tornado lifted a truck and dropped it in the next field.
examples.cn: 龙卷风把一辆卡车卷起，又把它扔到隔壁田里。

examples.en: Meteorologists count a funnel as a tornado only when it touches the ground.
examples.cn: 气象学家只有在漏斗云触地时才把它算作龙卷风。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「陀螺转」——像陀螺一样贴地狂转的风

root: 西班牙语 tronada「雷暴」（tronar「打雷」，拉丁 tonare「打雷」）与 tornado「旋转的」（tornar「转」，拉丁 tornare「转」）混合而成。英语 17 世纪借入时指海上雷暴，19 世纪才专指触地的漏斗云；词源清楚，义项收窄的年代有明确记载。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one funnel: the technical vortex, the everyday whirlwind, the old thunderstorm sense, the West African squall, the disaster, the metaphor, the season and the aircraft name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个漏斗展开：技术涡旋、日常旋风、旧雷暴义、西非飑线、灾害事件、比喻义、龙卷风季与飞机专名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark funnel hanging from a thundercloud and stirring dust at the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑色漏斗从雷暴云垂下，在地面搅起尘土。

branches.en: TECHNICAL AND EVERYDAY: one strict definition with ground contact, one loose name for any visible whirl.
branches.cn: 技术与日常：一个是要求触地的严格定义，一个是任何可见旋风的宽泛叫法。

branches.en: TWO OLD WEATHER SENSES: the English thunderstorm of the seventeenth century and the West African squall line keep the wider meaning.
branches.cn: 两个旧的天气义：17 世纪英语的雷暴与西非的飑线保留了更宽的含义。

branches.en: DISASTER AND CALENDAR: the event that destroys and the season that schedules it.
branches.cn: 灾害与日历：造成破坏的事件与为它排定时间的季节。

branches.en: SOCIAL BURST: applause and criticism can arrive with the same spin.
branches.cn: 社会爆发：掌声与批评能以同样的旋转到来。

branches.en: NAME REUSED: the storm word becomes a proper name for a combat aircraft.
branches.cn: 名称再用：风暴词成为战斗机的专名。

intro.en: Tornado has no English prefix or suffix; it is a borrowed Spanish blend. Its derivatives are compounds and the learned adjective tornadic.
intro.cn: tornado 没有英语前缀或后缀；它是借入的西班牙语混合词。其派生形式是复合词与学术形容词 tornadic。

latinIntro.en: Two Latin families meet in this word: tonare 'to thunder' and tornare 'to turn'. Both are genuine and both are visible in the Spanish forms.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词里汇合了两个拉丁词族：tonare「打雷」与 tornare「转」。两者都真实存在，且都能在西班牙语形式中看到。

items.structure: Spanish tronar 'to thunder', from Latin tonare
items.example: Spanish tronar 'to thunder' is the source of tronada, the older word for a storm.
items.exampleCN: 西班牙语 tronar「打雷」是 tronada（较早的风暴说法）的来源。

items.structure: Spanish tornar 'to turn', from Latin tornare
items.example: Spanish tornar 'to turn' gives tornado its rotating sense.
items.exampleCN: 西班牙语 tornar「转」赋予 tornado 旋转的含义。
这个词尾使 tornado 字面上就是「被转动的」。

items.example: Tornadic winds are the strongest on the Plains.
items.exampleCN: 龙卷风风力是平原上最强的。

items.example: Tornadogenesis began along the dry line.
items.exampleCN: 龙卷风生成在干线一带开始。

items.example: A tornado-like vortex formed over the lake.
items.exampleCN: 湖面上形成了一个龙卷风般的涡旋。
这个避难所是防龙卷风的。

items.example: The county is tornado-prone in spring.
items.exampleCN: 这个县春季易受龙卷风袭击。

latinEntries.meaning: to turn, to turn in a lathe
